descriptionHtml:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

About The Team

Anduril's Growth organization identifies, shapes, captures, and grows new opportunities for the company.

This role sits within the Connected Warfare Division. Connected Warfare builds the software and hardware substrate for global, multi-domain command and control (C2) — joint, time-sensitive, connected mesh ecosystems that link every robot, human, and sensor across every domain to close kill chains and enable mission autonomy. The division includes the Voyager team, which delivers ruggedised computing and communications platforms for the network edge.About the Job

  • This is a sales role. You are here to hunt and close new business for Connected Warfare across Europe and the Middle East.
  • Based in continental Europe, you'll report to the Head of Growth for Anduril's International Connected Warfare business. You carry initial responsibility for the region, with scope to expand as the business scales.
  • European defence environments come with sovereign requirements, legacy architectures, and security constraints. You will know these pain points cold and demonstrate how Anduril integrates with — and supercharges — the systems customers already operate.
  • The work is matrixed: you'll pull on programs, engineering, capture, software, finance, partners, and customers to win. The deliverable is unambiguous: pipeline, partners, and signed contracts. This is an individual-contributor role — no direct reports. Your impact is measured in the business you build and the contracts you close

What You’ll Do

  • Drive go-to-market. Stand up and execute the Connected Warfare growth strategy across Europe and the Middle East. Identify, qualify, shape, and close complex opportunities with Allied nations, navigating international procurement cycles and sovereign requirements to secure long-term programs of record.
  • Generate and capture new business. Run a dual-track motion: hunt and close net-new customers across the region while partnering with delivery teams to scale and expand current contracts.
  • Map customer requirements. Build a working understanding of regional defence requirements, security constraints, and legacy architectures. Show how Anduril's open architecture integrates with sovereign systems to solve real operational problems.
  • Build and manage the regional channel. Identify, onboard, and manage strategic partners, resellers, system integrators, and European primes. Coordinate with Anduril's Global Defense team on teaming agreements that accelerate adoption.
  • Run the internal matrix. Maintain close working relationships across business line and division leadership, growth, programs, engineering, and corporate functions to shape opportunities and unblock execution.
  • Deliver the number. Hit financial performance targets and build the multi-year plan to back them up. Provide leadership with long-term growth and product strategy for Connected Warfare in region.
  • Inform product. Translate region-specific mission profiles, sovereign cloud requirements, and degraded-network realities back into the product roadmap.
  • Represent Anduril. Communicate technical and operational value to senior military officials, procurement officers, and partners — articulating how Lattice-enabled C2 closes kill chains in contested environments

Growth Activities

  • Use Salesforce as the system of record — accounts, pricing, points of contact, expected close dates, and all customer activity
  • Partner with Sales Engineering to refine customer solutions
  • Perform live and static demonstrations on-site or via VTC
  • Create and deliver client presentations and proposals tailored to specific customer needs
  • Identify regional contract vehicles (e.g. NATO frameworks, national procurement programmes) and lead proposal development

Required Qualifications

  • 10+ years in defence, dual-use, or enterprise networking sales, with at least 5 years closing business with European government and military customers
  • A proven hunter: documented record of identifying, qualifying, and closing complex deals with European Ministries of Defence (MoDs), NATO bodies, or coalition partners — opened the door, shaped the requirement, closed the contract
  • Deep familiarity with European defence procurement cycles, budgeting, and sovereign security frameworks

descriptionHtml:
About Baringa 

Baringa is a global consulting firm that partners with leaders to drive change and create value. With deep industry expertise, and enabled by advanced technology, the firm helps clients to deliver with greater confidence and certainty. With over 2,000 people across the UK, Europe, North America, Asia and Australia, the firm combines global insight with local understanding.

The firm works across energy and resources, financial services, government and public sector, consumer products and retail, pharmaceuticals and life sciences, manufacturing, and technology, media and telecoms, with capabilities spanning strategy, transformation and operational excellence – all powered by advanced technology, data, AI and digital innovation.

Clients value Baringa’s collaborative approach and the way its teams integrate seamlessly – all working with a shared understanding of what matters most. The firm is known for its kind, curious experts who listen closely and care deeply about client success as they help clients transform energy markets, modernise financial platforms, expand telecoms and digital networks through advanced data analytics, enable digital services in government, and unlock growth in consumer sectors.

Certified as a Great Place to Work around the world, Baringa has been recognised by the Financial Times in 22 categories of its UK Leading Management Consultants rankings, and by Forbes for four consecutive years as one of the World’s Best Management Consulting Firms.

Our Insurance practice is looking for an experienced Director or Senior Manager to help deliver and grow our Health Insurance and Insurance Technology Transformation capability.

Baringa helps insurers define their strategy, deliver complex change and modernise their platforms, data and operating models. We are growing our presence with leading UK health insurers and developing a cross-Baringa Health Insurance proposition. At the same time, we are building our Insurance Technology Transformation capability to support Global P&C carriers and clients across the wider Insurance sector.

As a Director or Senior Manager, you will combine Health Insurance expertise with strong technology transformation experience, client leadership, programme delivery and business development. You will lead complex workstreams and engagements, build trusted relationships with senior stakeholders, support the development of client opportunities and help grow our people, propositions and market profile. Your primary focus will be our Health Insurance agenda, but your skills will transfer to our Global P&C and wider Insurance technology transformation work.

title: Director Go-to-Market and Revenue Strategy
descriptionHtml:
Who We Are

You've ordered dinner through Just Eat Takeaway. You've bought and sold on OLX. You've paid with PayU. Chances are, you've already used a Prosus company today.

We are Prosus, a global technology company powering some of the world's leading lifestyle ecommerce businesses. Every day, billions of people across India, Latin America, Europe and beyond use our products and services to buy, sell, pay, connect and discover.

Our AI-driven ecosystem spans 100+ companies across ecommerce, food delivery, fintech and experiences, serving billions of consumers worldwide. AI powers how we operate and innovate, with more than 60,000 active AI agents helping our teams build, scale and move faster. Through our investment team, we also back the founders and technologies shaping the future: From robotics and autonomous systems to synthetic biology and frontier AI.

Guided by our five values Innovation, Results, People, Impact, and Entrepreneurship, culture is our competitive advantage. We thrive with experimentation; we build, we test, we learn, we iterate.

Join us in shaping the future of technology at global scale.

WHO YOU ARE

You are a commercial leader who has built the go-to-market of a platform from a blank page and knows what it takes to turn a product that people already use into a business that pays for itself. You have priced and packaged products for marketplaces, brands or merchants, and you have seen the difference between a model that looks good in a spreadsheet and one that a small business owner actually adopts.

You are comfortable in a B2B2C world: the customer is reached through someone else's channel, the data belongs to the ecosystem, and the money comes from several ends of a transaction at once. You influence without authority, because the teams that execute will rarely report to you. You are rigorous with numbers and plain with people, and you are at ease saying what the evidence shows even when the room expects something else.

You want to build something that reaches millions of small businesses, you are prepared to work for it.

THE OPPORTUNITY

Toqan for Partners is the AI assistant for the merchants across the companies of the Prosus ecosystem: restaurants, pharmacies, hotels, sellers, real estate agencies and car dealers, five million businesses in total. It launched to restaurants on iFood in Brazil in September 2026 and reached 65,000 restaurants in four weeks with no media spend.

The next twelve months decide how it will become a business: which applications partners pay for and at what price, how value is shared with everyone the partner transacts with, how the uplift is measured and published so the next company embeds, and how the product travels from iFood to the rest of the ecosystem and to India and Europe. You will lead that work, as the owner of the go-to-market and the revenue strategy of Toqan for Partners, alongside the product and technology leads who own what gets built.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

Own the commercial model

Define pricing and packaging for the applications partners pay for, media management, supply, finance and operations, at a fraction of what they spend today and justified by the return they see. Design how Toqan takes part in the value it creates for the other end: take rate on agent-negotiated supply, credit origination, brand and industry media, and cross-sell of the ecosystem companies' own products. Set the rules that keep it honest, starting with the separation between paid placement and recommendation.

Drive the rollout across the ecosystem

With the Head of Operations, secure the commitment of each business in the ecosystem: sponsor, distribution, conditional yes and first market. Run the rollout inside each one, working through the teams that own the merchant relationship, and bring the product to its next verticals and markets.

Build the measurement

Own the scoreboard: active partners under a strict definition, uplift per business in retention and GMV, cost and value per active partner. Make the uplift the argument that brings the next company in and the evidence behind every pricing decision.

Structure the partnerships that carry the revenue

Lead the commercial agreements with distributors, industry, fintechs and the ecosystem companies' commercial platforms, from first conversation to signed terms, and the co-investment models that align their incentives with the partner's.

Build and lead the team

Hire and develop a small go-to-market and revenue team, growth on the merchant side, monetisation and analytics, and set its standard for rigour, ownership and candour.

WHAT YOU BRING

  • Ten or more years in go-to-market, revenue or commercial strategy, with at least one commercial function built from scratch and grown to scale.

  • Hands-on experience with pricing and packaging, ideally for marketplaces, retail media, payments or SaaS sold to small businesses.

  • Experience on more than one side of a marketplace: merchants or sellers, brands or suppliers, the platform itself.

  • A track record of adoption at scale with a long tail of small customers, not only of large enterprise deals.

  • Proven ability to move a result through teams that do not report to you, and to work inside another company's channel.

  • Fluency with data: you build the business case, run the analysis and read the uplift yourself, and use AI tooling as a normal part of how you work.

  • Candour, humility and patience: you say what the numbers say, you arrive to learn before you teach.

  • English required; Portuguese or Spanish strongly preferred.

WHAT WE OFFER

  • Global impact: a product that reaches five million small businesses across Latin America, Europe and India.

  • Ownership: the commercial model of a new business, with the numbers to be judged on and the autonomy to build it.

  • Growth: exposure to the leadership of the group and of its companies, and a clear path into operating roles in the ecosystem.

  • Competitive compensation and the Prosus benefits package for the location of the role.

Why Prosus?

At Prosus, your colleagues include 60,000 AI agents… and your job is to figure out what that actually means. We're one of the largest operators of agentic AI on the planet, inside a $100B+ portfolio across 100+ companies and two billion people. The humans here own what AI can't do alone: judgment, creativity, and the call on what gets built next.

Own the impact. Work the ecosystem. Earn your growth. Build with backing.

Curious about our perks and benefits? Take a look at this page.

Our Diversity & Inclusion Commitment

We respect the dignity and human rights of individuals and communities wherever we operate in the world. Building an inclusive workplace where everyone feels welcome and can thrive is critical for us. We provide access to education, which helps everyone understand the important role they play and the positive impact they can have.

Want to know more about life at Prosus? Explore our culture and values.

title: Director, International Expansion — CEO Office
descriptionHtml:
About Airwallex

Airwallex is the AI-native financial operating system for a real-time, intelligent economy. More than 675,000 businesses, including McLaren Racing, Qantas, SHEIN, and TikTok, use us, directly or through our platform partners, to run their financial operations or build and monetize financial products of their own.

We started in Melbourne in 2015 to build the infrastructure global commerce runs on. We're the regulated backbone behind global payments: not by accident, but by design. A decade plus, 85+ licenses, and a financial infrastructure spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.

We're co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore, with more than 2,700 people across 27 offices. We hire builders with founder-level energy, people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told what to do. Read our operating principles to see it in full.

 

About the team

The CEO Office partners directly with Airwallex's executive leadership on the company's most important priorities. We work across regions and functions to shape the company's direction, solve complex problems, and turn ambitious ideas into reality.

International expansion is a core strategic priority for Airwallex. As we continue to build a truly global financial platform, we are expanding into new markets, securing regulatory licences, deepening our local financial infrastructure, and bringing new products to customers around the world.

We operate at the intersection of strategy, regulation, product, and execution, working closely with leaders across Product, Engineering, Legal, Risk, Finance, and Operations. The team combines strategic thinking with an entrepreneurial, hands-on approach to building and scaling our international presence.

What you'll do

As Director, International Expansion, you will lead Airwallex's expansion into new markets globally, shaping where and how we grow and building the regulatory, product, and operational foundations to succeed.

You will own a portfolio of market-entry initiatives end to end, from evaluating opportunities and defining entry strategies through licensing, product localisation, operational readiness, and commercial launch.

Reporting to the CEO's Chief of Staff, you will lead a lean team and work directly with senior executives to influence strategic decisions, mobilise cross-functional teams, and overcome the complex challenges of entering new markets.

This is a high-impact leadership role for someone who combines strategic judgment, an entrepreneurial mindset, and the ability to translate ambitious plans into tangible outcomes. You will build and lead the expansion function while remaining directly involved in the most strategically important and complex market-entry initiatives.

Responsibilities

  • Lead global expansion strategy: Own the strategy and execution of Airwallex's expansion into new markets globally. Evaluate and prioritise market opportunities, define entry strategies, and recommend where and how Airwallex should invest to establish and scale its presence.

  • Own market entry end to end: Lead expansion initiatives from initial market assessment through regulatory authorisation, entity establishment, product readiness, and operational launch. Take accountability for delivering market entries and navigating the strategic and execution challenges along the way.

  • Define regulatory and operating models: Work closely with Legal, Compliance, Risk, and Finance to determine the optimal licensing, legal entity, and operating structures for each market. Translate regulatory requirements into practical, scalable business models that support Airwallex's long-term ambitions.

  • Influence product and infrastructure strategy: Partner with Product and Engineering leadership to shape local product capabilities, payment infrastructure, and market-specific roadmaps. Identify opportunities to deepen Airwallex's presence through new licences, direct payment-system access, and expanded product offerings.

  • Lead a high-performing team: Manage and develop a lean team, setting clear priorities, providing strategic guidance, and driving accountability across multiple markets. Personally lead the highest-priority or most complex initiatives while building the team's capabilities.

  • Drive executive alignment and investment decisions: Work directly with the CEO's Chief of Staff and senior executives to shape expansion priorities, resolve critical trade-offs, secure resources, and drive timely decisions. Present clear recommendations on market opportunities, regulatory strategy, investment requirements, and launch readiness.

  • Build external relationships: Partner with local regulators, financial institutions, payment networks, advisers, and other strategic stakeholders to support regulatory approvals, establish local capabilities, and unlock new market opportunities.

  • Build a scalable expansion engine: Develop repeatable frameworks, tools, and operating processes that enable Airwallex to expand faster and more efficiently. Leverage AI and automation to improve regulatory intelligence, market analysis, execution tracking, and cross-functional coordination.

  • Drive broader CEO Office priorities: Support or lead high-impact strategic initiatives beyond international expansion, working across the business to solve complex problems, shape company-level decisions, and drive execution on critical priorities.

Who you are

Minimum qualifications:

  • Intellectually curious, resilient, and hungry to win. You thrive on solving difficult problems, challenge conventional thinking, learn quickly, and have the drive and persistence to turn ambitious goals into results.

  • Significant experience in strategy, international expansion, business operations, or related roles, ideally in fintech, payments, banking, or other high-growth technology businesses.

  • Strong strategic and commercial judgment, with the ability to navigate ambiguity, evaluate complex trade-offs, and translate big-picture thinking into practical execution.

  • Demonstrated ability to lead teams and complex cross-functional initiatives, influence senior stakeholders, and drive outcomes in fast-paced environments.

  • Exceptional analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills, with the ability to simplify complexity, make sound decisions, and engage effectively with executive leadership.

  • Entrepreneurial, hands-on mindset with a strong sense of ownership and willingness to get into the details to make things happen.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Proven track record of leading international market entries, including regulatory licensing, market-entry strategy, and operational launches.

  • Experience in fintech, payments, or financial services, with an understanding of regulatory frameworks, financial infrastructure, and the interplay between licensing, product, and commercial strategy.

  • Experience building and leading high-performing teams in high-growth, cross-functional environments.

Applicant Safety Policy: Fraud and Third-Party Recruiters

To protect you from recruitment scams, please be aware that Airwallex will not ask for bank details, sensitive ID numbers (i.e. passport), or any form of payment during the application or interview process. All official communication will come from an @airwallex.com email address. Please apply only through careers.airwallex.com or our official LinkedIn page.

Airwallex does not accept unsolicited resumes from search firms/recruiters. Airwallex will not pay any fees to search firms/recruiters if a candidate is submitted by a search firm/recruiter unless an agreement has been entered into with respect to specific open position(s). Search firms/recruiters submitting resumes to Airwallex on an unsolicited basis shall be deemed to accept this condition, regardless of any other provision to the contrary.

Equal opportunity

Airwallex is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and anyone seeking employment at Airwallex is considered based on merit, qualifications, competence and talent. We don’t regard color, religion, race, national origin, sexual orientation, ancestry, citizenship, sex, marital or family status, disability, gender, or any other legally protected status when making our hiring decisions. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know.

We're looking for a Director, Slate Operations to own this end to end. There are two sides to it: keeping the Group running as an organization — its cadence, process, and the day-to-day support the Game Board, Head of Slate Development and leadership team rely on — and running program management for the Game Development Framework (GDF) so games move cleanly from concept to launch. You'll sit inside the Slate Development Group but work with every part of Scopely: game teams, divisional leadership, finance, strategy, and corporate development.

  • Be the operational point of contact for specific in-development games — running the GDF cadence and connecting game and central teams so decisions get made once and aren't re-litigated. The main goal is to be the end to end steward for game teams in the game development framework.
  • Deliver operational excellence within our internal team, shaping our service model, priorities, and ways of working. Evolve our capabilities as needs change.
  • Drive the cross-slate operating model so independent game teams reuse what already works instead of rebuilding it.
  • Bring structure to consequential decisions — organize the inputs, assumptions, and trade-offs early so the owners and the room can reach real alignment before committing.
  • Own a capstone project — one meaty area you drive end to end, for example: evolving the GDF, owning launch readiness, or operationalizing central partnerships, depending on where the need is. 
  • Keep investment decisions well-informed — track progress across games at different stages, and surface Greenlight Case, budget, staffing, and dependency status so leadership can challenge and decide.
  • Unblock teams through the development cycle, especially at launch readiness, by clearing operational issues with central partners (legal, IT, procurement, finance, logistics) so teams stay focused on the game. Partner with marketing, strategy, and divisional leadership so launches go out clean.
  • Give teams operational support — production perspective, process, facilitation, and help navigating the GDF.
  • Operationalize playtests and validation — help build and run research, playtest, and validation plans, and package the findings so vertical owners and leaders can form the recommendation.
  • Utilize the latest AI technologies to keep information flowing — the dashboards, status, and key dates people need to see, without the overhead.

What We’re Looking For: 

  • Bachelor's degree, MBA a plus — or the equivalent in experience.
  • 10+ years in program/project management across tech and direct-to-consumer businesses, at least 5 of them in games, working within or alongside a development team.
  • You know how games get made and sold — development, publishing, platforms, business models. You don't need to have shipped one yourself, but you get what game teams are up against.
  • You've supported senior execs in a fast-moving environment and you like the pace — taking initiative, juggling priorities, switching gears without losing the thread.
  • You can run a lot of projects at once, ideally a mix of R&D and live.
  • You're comfortable in ambiguity and good at creating clarity for other people. You make sound calls in the company's interest and know when to escalate.
  • You can hold your own with P&Ls and free-to-play KPIs.
  • You spot the process that's slowing people down and fix it — and you'll push back and start the right debate when it matters.
  • You build trust with all kinds of people at every level and don't flinch at the hard conversations — with the presence to grow into a partner to senior game leaders over time.
  • You write clearly and fast, and you can build a strong deck with cross-functional input.
  • Detail and organization come naturally to you.
  • Low ego, business outcomes first, open to feedback — and genuinely curious about every part of the business.
  • You play games and care about the industry.

About Scopely

Scopely is a leading video game and global interactive entertainment company, home to many of the world’s most beloved and enduring experiences, including two of the most successful mobile games of all-time “MONOPOLY GO!” and “Pokémon GO,” along with “Stumble Guys,” “Star Trek™ Fleet Command,” “MARVEL Strike Force,” “WWE Champions,” the Scrabble® franchise, “Yahtzee® With Buddies,” and many others. Across mobile, web, PC, and console, Scopely creates, develops, publishes, and live-operates one of the most diversified and award-winning portfolios in the games industry — bringing hundreds of millions of players together through a shared love of play.

Founded in 2011, Scopely is powered by its exceptional team — including thousands of world-class gamemakers around the globe, a distinctive tenet-driven culture, and its proprietary technology platform, Playgami. Together, these strengths have fueled Scopely’s position as the #1 mobile games company in the U.S. and #2 globally, generating more than $10 billion in lifetime revenue. Whether building global sensations like “MONOPOLY GO!” from the ground up, or expanding through strategic acquisitions, including the FoxNext, GSN, and Scopely Explore games businesses — Scopely consistently delivers experiences players love today and return to for years to come.

Recognized multiple times as one of the "100 Most Influential Companies in the World" by TIME magazine and one of Fast Company's "World's Most Innovative Companies" and “Best Workplaces for Innovators,” Scopely believes that video games can be a force for good — creating meaningful connections, vibrant communities, and making life better through play.

Scopely has global operations and partners across four continents in more than a dozen countries worldwide. For more information, visit: https://www.scopely.com/.

title: Director, Partnerships
descriptionHtml:
About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

Ramp is building it's UK business from the ground up. You will work closely with the UK go-to-market team and cross-functional leaders across Sales, Product, Marketing, and Customer Success to make partnerships a meaningful driver of market entry and long-term growth.

title: Electronics Engineering Manager
descriptionHtml:
About IonQ: 

IonQ, Inc. [NYSE: IONQ] is the world’s leading quantum platform and merchant supplier - delivering integrated quantum solutions across computing, networking, sensing, and security. IonQ’s newest generation of quantum computers, the IonQ Tempo, is the latest in a line of cutting-edge systems that have been helping customers and partners including Amazon Web Services, and AstraZeneca achieve 20x performance results and accelerate innovation in drug discovery, materials science, financial modeling, logistics, cybersecurity, and defense. In 2025, the company achieved 99.99% two-qubit gate fidelity, setting a world record in quantum computing performance.

Headquartered in College Park, Maryland, IonQ has operations in California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Tennessee, Washington, Italy, South Korea, Sweden, Switzerland, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Our quantum computing services are available through all major cloud providers, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space. IonQ is making quantum platforms more accessible and impactful than ever before.  

The Role

We are looking for an Electronics Engineering Manager to lead the electronics function within our Systems team at IonQ. You will lead a team of three electronics engineers and grow it as our programmes scale. The team designs, builds and tests the electronics subsystems behind our mission to build the most performant quantum computers.

This is a player-coach role, with roughly 60% of your time spent leading the team and 40% on hands-on design work. You will set the technical direction for our electronics deliverables and build a team that can deliver them reliably, from experimental prototypes to rack-ready production systems.

Responsibilities 

You will own the electronics roadmap for current and next-generation quantum systems. That covers schematic capture and PCB layout through to board and system-level test, and the drive architecture for QPU designs.

You will balance hands-on technical leadership with people management, planning and coordination across teams. As the main electronics contact for the physics, firmware, mechanical and systems teams, you will turn complex physical requirements into clear, achievable engineering plans, and you will keep improving the tooling, workflow and capability of the team.Key responsibilities include: 

  • Team leadership: Lead and develop a team of three electronics engineers and play a key role in growing it through hiring. Set clear goals, run regular 1:1s and performance reviews, and build a culture of technical excellence and accountability.
  • Technical direction: Own the architecture of the electronics subsystems, including mixed-signal design, high-speed digital and signal integrity. Approve key design decisions and lead design reviews.
  • Delivery and planning: Plan, prioritise and track electronics workstreams against programme milestones, managing resourcing, schedules, risks and dependencies, and report progress to stakeholders.
  • Quality and process: Set and improve design standards, review processes, verification and test strategy (simulation, bench test, system integration) and documentation practices.
  • Productisation: Lead the move from experimental prototypes to robust, manufacturable, rack-ready production systems, working with suppliers and contract manufacturers as needed.

Requirements 

To succeed, you will need around ten years of experience in electronics design, with a strong background in high-speed and mixed-signal electronics, proven experience leading engineers and a track record of taking hardware from concept through prototype to production on schedule. You should be able to give credible technical guidance while growing the team around you, and bring a high level of attention to detail to your own work and to the designs you review.

You will be comfortable in a fast-moving, highly technical environment and know when to use waterfall or agile delivery in a hardware setting. Experience with Jira and Smartsheet, exposure to cryogenic environments, RF/microwave engineering (up to 500 MHz) or Python-based test automation, and familiarity with the Sinara/ARTIQ ecosystem in a quantum or physics research setting would all be an advantage.


You’d be a great fit with:

  • Engineering leadership experience: A track record of managing or technically leading electronics engineers, including hiring, mentoring and performance management.
  • Strong hardware design background: Hands-on experience with mixed-signal and high-speed digital design, SPICE modelling and lab verification (oscilloscopes, spectrum analysers).
  • Altium expertise: Experience with complex schematics, rigid-flex designs and advanced signal-integrity constraints, and the ability to review and guide others' designs.
  • FPGA and high-performance hardware: Familiarity with Xilinx/Intel toolchains (Vivado/Quartus) and carriers such as the BittWare XUP series or Sinara/ARTIQ hardware.
  • High-speed interfaces: Knowledge of SFP+/QSFP-DD interfaces, 10/100G Ethernet and high-speed differential pair routing.

Compensation will vary based on individual factors such as education, qualifications, and experience of the final candidate(s), specific office location, and calibration against relevant market data and internal team equity. Posted base salary figures are subject to change as new market data becomes available. Our benefits include comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans, matching 401(k), unlimited PTO and paid holidays, parental/adoption leave, legal insurance, and a home technology stipend. Details of participation in these benefit plans will be provided when a candidate receives an offer of employment.

title: Employer Brand Strategist
descriptionHtml:
In short: one of Conduct's first marketing hires, owning employer brand and our talent community. You will make the case, to exceptional people in every function, for why Conduct is where they should do their life's work.

Why Conduct

The world's largest companies compete by being different, and most of that difference lives in software they built for themselves. It decides how parcels reach your door and how food reaches the supermarket. That software is their advantage. It is also the hardest thing in the business to change safely, so good ideas wait months, sometimes years, for the systems to catch up.

Every large enterprise has a software company hiding inside it. Conduct is building its operating system. It reads a company's code and processes, works out what has to change, and helps the business and its systems move together. We start with SAP, and go wherever custom software has grown too complex to change safely.

Rio Tinto, Daimler Truck, and DHL already trust us with their most critical systems. We have signed partnerships with major systems integrators, just raised a $60M Series A, and demand is ahead of what we can serve.

We are a talent-dense team doing our life's work in London and New York. Extreme ownership, high velocity, low-ego collaboration. What you build here shapes the company, and how the world's largest companies operate.

About the role

We're looking for someone to own employer brand and talent community as part of the founding marketing team. Hiring exceptional people fast enough is the biggest challenge Conduct faces. We're scaling from about 70 people to 500, across engineering, deployment strategy, go-to-market and operations, and every one of those candidates needs to understand why Conduct matters.

You will articulate why Conduct matters to talent: who we are, what we care about, why the product matters and where it is going. You will take the case the founders make for the company's ambition and turn it into something every candidate hears, from the careers page to the final interview. You will work closely with the talent team on candidate experience, and with our Social & Community Lead, who owns our social channels and developer community, to bring the employer brand to life online.

You will also build Conduct's talent community: the people who aren't ready to join yet but should be one day. You will design recruiting and talent events across every function, and relationships that keep great people close.

What you'll do

  • Tell the talent story. Write the talent narrative: why work at Conduct, the opportunity areas and the vision, with a clear story for each function we hire into.

  • Own the careers experience. The careers page, job descriptions, candidate materials and everything we say to candidates.

  • Shape candidate experience. Work with the talent team on a consistent, high-touch process, from candidate prep packs to how the founders' case for Conduct shows up in every interview.

  • Create employer brand content. Produce films, stories and assets that show what it is really like to work here, for the Social & Community Lead to amplify on our channels.

  • Build our talent community. Design recruiting events, talent dinners and programmes that keep great people close until the timing is right.

  • Shape partner events. Combine thought leadership with recruiting at events with partners like Anthropic, OpenAI and Legora, with Owned Events leading production.

  • Welcome new joiners. Create a values document and welcome pack for new Conductors, in partnership with internal comms.

What we're looking for

  • A generalist with sharp taste and a relentless drive to ship. You have built things before (brands, communities, events, side projects) and you have strong opinions on what great looks like. You see a gap and fill it.

  • Exceptional writing and editing. This is the most important skill for the role.

  • A clear spike in employer brand, and the range to contribute across the wider marketing team.

  • A track record of building an employer brand or talent community that helped a company hire, ideally across technical and commercial roles.

  • Experience at a fast-moving tech company, and comfort with a broad mandate and the pace that comes with it.

  • The ability to make things yourself, in words, video and visuals, rather than only brief them.

  • Genuine conviction about the problem Conduct solves. Experience in enterprise software or AI is a strong plus.

  • A bias to action. You are hands-on whatever your seniority.

  • An appetite for being in the office every day, close to the team and the work.

Your seniority does not matter. Ambition, craft and the ability to turn ideas into high-quality work quickly do. We sponsor visas from everywhere. We're convinced diverse teams build better products, and we especially encourage people from groups underrepresented in tech to reach out.

title: Energy Procurement & Policy
descriptionHtml:
About Mistral

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

The team

Mistral Cloud builds and operates the infrastructure that powers Mistral's AI. The Data Centers team signs long-term leases for data center capacity developed by third-party operators, sources the GPUs that fill those halls, and runs the workloads that train and serve Mistral's models. Today the team is around 40 people, mainly based in Paris with some remote members, and operates roughly 200 MW of existing capacity across France. Key partners include Éclairion in France and EcoDC in Sweden, which is currently delivering Mistral's first Swedish data center.

The team sits at the center of an ambitious roadmap: Mistral has publicly committed to securing one gigawatt of data center capacity globally by 2030. With 200 MW already online, roughly 800 MW remain to be secured over the next five years. Every megawatt needs power, and power is this role's domain.

The Role

Mistral's data centers will consume hundreds of megawatts of electricity. This hire makes sure that power is reliable and affordable. You will define and execute Mistral's energy procurement strategy: structuring agreements with utilities, hedging against volatile spot prices, and tracking the regulatory changes that affect where and how data centers can be powered. The role also touches energy policy and community relations in the regions where Mistral operates.

This is a hybrid seat. Roughly half of the work is commercial: procurement contracts, hedging instruments, and price risk management. The other half is policy and positioning: monitoring regulation, engaging with grid operators and local authorities, and helping Mistral build the social license to operate large data centers across Europe.

What You Will Do

  • Define and execute Mistral's energy procurement strategy across European data center sites

  • Negotiate power purchase agreements and procurement contracts with utilities

  • Structure hedging agreements to limit exposure to volatile spot power prices

  • Monitor energy regulation and policy developments that affect data center siting, grid connection, and power pricing

  • Engage with grid operators, regulators, and local communities in regions where Mistral builds and operates data centers

What We're Looking For

  • You have procured energy at scale. You have structured power purchase agreements, utility contracts, or hedging instruments for industrial or infrastructure-scale consumers.

  • You understand European energy markets. You know how power pricing, grid connection, and regulation work across the markets where Mistral operates.

  • You can read a regulatory brief. You have tracked and interpreted energy or infrastructure policy and translated it into commercial implications.

  • You communicate across disciplines. You work effectively with engineers, finance, legal, and external stakeholders, and can explain complex energy concepts to non-specialists.

What We Offer

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page.

Privacy Policy

Your privacy matters to us. You can learn more about how we handle your personal data in our Applicant Privacy Policy.

title: Engineering Delivery & Operations Manager
descriptionHtml:
Joining Weezevent means working on tangible solutions used at international festivals (Hellfest, Boomtown, Tomorrowland, Lollapalooza, Boom), major sporting events (Formula 1, the Olympic Games, Euro fan zones), and high-volume live experiences.

Weezevent builds the technology behind live events: ticketing, cashless payment, CRM, staff solutions and access control. We are about 100 people in the tech team (engineering and product organisation), part of a group that has grown both organically and through acquisitions, so our teams span several countries and cultures.

We are at an inflection point. We are opening a focused 12–18 month window to invest heavily in the foundations of our main product, WeezTicket: paying down technical debt, tightening our architecture, and setting ourselves up for the next phase of growth. To run that program, we’re hiring an Engineering Delivery & Operations Manager (M/F, based in Clichy) to own its delivery.

Vos missions

This is a two-part role, and the first part is where you’ll spend most of your first year.

Part one : deliver the program. A board of our most experienced engineers is defining the architectural direction and producing a large backlog of clean-up and improvement work. That work will be delivered by several external squads brought in for the program. You own the delivery layer between them: getting squads stood up and productive on time, tracking each one’s pace and quality, and keeping the whole program on schedule.

  • Stand up and onboard external squads, around 20 developers across 5 to 6 squads, on time : access, environments, documentation, and a well-scoped first backlog ready before they start
  • Track the delivery pace of each squad against its commitments, and keep a clear program-level view of what’s on track, slipping, or blocked
  • Hold squads to the quality bar set by the architectural board : tests, reviews, and no new debt introduced while removing old debt
  • Manage cross-squad dependencies so work lands in the right order
  • Track program spend against budget and manage the relationships with the partners supplying the squads
  • Report program status to the CTO and the board on a regular cadence

Part two : become the operational backbone of engineering. As the program matures, you’ll take on the people-operations side of the organisation: helping our managers run great 1:1s and reviews, coordinating the performance cycle, keeping an eye on team capacity and wellbeing, and bringing rigour to tooling and budget. This is what makes the role a long-term home rather than a temporary program job.

You’ll work closely with the CTO, the architectural board, our 4 Team Leads, and the external partners supplying the squads. You won’t set the technical strategy or write the code, you’ll make sure the right work gets delivered, on time, at the right quality.

  • Help 4 Team Leads and 6 Squad Leads run consistent 1:1s and grow as managers
  • Coordinate the performance review cycle and make sure follow-up actions actually happen
  • Keep visibility on team capacity, absences, and early signals of overload or burnout
  • Bring structure to tech budget tracking and to the governance of our tools and licences
  • Support hiring and internal mobility alongside our recruitment team

Vos compétences

Must-haves

  • Experience running a multi-squad delivery program end to end: ideally involving external agencies, consultancies, or contract teams
  • A track record of onboarding external teams onto an existing codebase and getting them productive quickly
  • Comfort owning a backlog, a schedule, and a budget across several parallel workstreams at once
  • The ability to track pace and quality per team and raise problems early, with data
  • Genuine tech literacy: you understand what developers do, can navigate a Jira board, and know what technical debt actually means
  • Fluent French and English

What makes you a strong long-term fit

  • Some experience coaching or supporting managers, or running a performance cycle in a tech company
  • A background that touched engineering, delivery, project management, or product before moving toward operations
  • Analytical rigour: you’re comfortable with numbers, dashboards, and cost reports
  • Direct, honest communication and real discretion with sensitive information

Nice to have

  • A third language (German or Dutch is a real plus given our footprint)
  • Experience working across France, the UK, the Netherlands, or Germany, and an understanding of how management styles differ across them

This is not

  • A role that sets architecture or writes code; that’s the board and the squads
  • A pure recruiter or a corporate-HR profile with no delivery or engineering exposure
  • A process-for-process’s-sake job. We want impact, not bureaucracy

The recruitment process

  • HR interview - background and soft skills
  • Interview with CTO - technical discussion

All our positions are open to people with disabilities.

Why it's a good move

You’ll run a high-visibility program with the direct backing of the CTO and the most senior engineers in the company, in an organisation that has decided to genuinely invest in its technical foundations rather than just talk about it. And when the program lands, you’ll have built yourself a permanent, central role at the heart of how our engineering organisation runs.

Engineering at Monzo

Monzo has successfully launched in Ireland and is expanding across Europe. We're now entering the next phase of our journey: building and scaling a multi-market European bank.

The EU Engineering organisation sits at the centre of that ambition. We are responsible for helping Monzo launch, grow and operate across Europe, navigating everything from product-market fit and customer growth to regulatory requirements, localisation and operational scale.

Unlike most engineering organisations at Monzo, EU does not own a single product area. We work horizontally across the company, partnering with teams across Payments, Core Banking, Growth, Wealth, Customer Operations, Fincrime, Platform and many others to bring Monzo's products to new markets and deliver great customer experiences locally.

As an Engineering Director, you'll lead a distributed engineering organisation across the UK, Spain and remote locations. You'll partner closely with Product, Design, Data, Operations, Risk, Compliance and executive stakeholders to solve complex problems that span organisational boundaries.

Success in this role comes through influence, relationships and organisational leadership as much as execution. You'll need to build alignment across a wide range of teams, create clarity in ambiguity, and help Monzo discover what works in new markets while establishing the foundations that allow us to scale across Europe.

This is one of Monzo's most strategically important areas and a unique opportunity to help build a European bank from the ground up.

What you’ll work on

  • You have experience scaling organisations through periods of rapid growth, organisational change or market expansion.

The interview process

At all stages we’ll create space for you to ask as many questions as you have, you’re interviewing us as well!

title: Engineering Lead
descriptionHtml:
ABOUT FLOCK

Road accidents kill and injure people, damage vehicles, and cost businesses fortunes. But traditional insurance does nothing to prevent them - it just pays out claims when they happen. At Flock, we’re changing that. Using telematics, AI, and real-time data, we proactively help our fleet customers prevent crashes. We obsessively focus on keeping drivers safe, and we put our money where our mouth is - paying out millions of pounds per year to fleets that get safer over time.

We were acquired by Admiral in May 2026. Now we combine the backing of the UK’s leading motor insurer with startup energy and speed. We’re growing fast with bigger plans than ever, and we’re hugely optimistic that our approach will save many more lives in the decade ahead.

We’re on a mission to make the world quantifiably safer. Join us!

We’re an AI-first business, so whatever the role, we want people who reach for AI by default, stay curious about what it can do, and use it to work faster and think bigger.

You’ll also shape how the team uses AI tools and coding agents to ship faster without lowering the quality bar.

WHAT WE THINK IS MOST EXCITING ABOUT THE ROLE:

Lead a team building products that directly drive Flock’s growth

  • Own delivery and technical quality for the Acquisition team, working hand in hand with the PM to ship features that directly impact how fleets find and choose Flock.

  • Write high-quality, well-tested TypeScript and own end-to-end delivery to production

Partner with product to drive impact

Grow engineers around you

  • Lead by example through code, design discussions and pairing.

  • Coach and mentor engineers across the team to raise standards and share ownership of technical direction.

Shape how the team works, not just what it builds

  • Drive improvements to developer experience, CI/CD, observability and release practices that make the whole team faster and more confident.

  • Make pragmatic trade-offs that balance reliability, performance and cost across AWS services.

  • Decide how the team uses AI, from coding assistants to agent workflows in review and release, keeping engineering judgement where it matters.

Curious how we build the future of fleet insurance? Dive into our Product & Engineering Blog, packed with technical deep-dives, behind-the-scenes stories, and real insights from the team you’d be joining.

A LITTLE MORE ON WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING:

As an Engineering Lead at Flock you’ll own delivery and technical direction for the Acquisition team, co-leading with the PM to ship products that directly drive growth, while raising the bar for the engineers around you.

API-Driven Development

  • Integrate with and contribute to the development of RESTful APIs exposed via API Gateway.

Serverless & Cloud Infrastructure

  • Use your AWS experience (Lambda, API Gateway, SQS, EventBridge, DynamoDB, S3, CloudWatch) to support and extend the Acquisition team’s services and pipelines.

  • Work with infrastructure-as-code tools like Terraform or CDK for provisioning and managing cloud resources.

Collaboration & Agile Delivery

  • Co-own the team’s success with the PM, jointly leading projects from scoping and planning through to delivery and measuring impact.

  • Give engineers the space and ownership to lead projects themselves, asking the right questions to challenge their thinking and help them land on the right solution.

Code Quality & Technical Standards

  • Deliver high-quality, well-tested code and act as a force-multiplier, raising standards through code reviews, pairing and design discussions.

  • Champion practical testing, type-safe APIs and pragmatic patterns that shape long-term technical direction across the team.

  • Set the example on AI-assisted development and coach engineers on where it genuinely speeds the team up and where human judgement needs to stay in the loop.

Working closely with your PM, you’ll bring clarity to complex problems and help define sharply scoped, impactful deliverables. Your success won’t be measured by your own output alone, but by the output, quality and growth of the whole team around you.

WHAT YOU’LL BRING TO FLOCK:

ESSENTIAL

  • Proven ability to co-lead a team alongside a PM, taking joint ownership of delivery, quality and outcomes, not just your own output.

  • Strong hands-on engineering ability; comfortable shipping high-quality, well-tested TypeScript in production and holding the team to the same standard.

  • Significant experience with AWS and modern serverless (Lambda, API Gateway, SQS, EventBridge, DynamoDB, S3, CloudWatch) or other cloud platforms.

  • A pragmatic approach to technical decisions, balancing reliability, observability, performance and cost, and bringing engineers along on the reasoning.

  • Track record of raising engineering standards as a force-multiplier, through code reviews, pairing, design discussions and shaping long-term technical direction.

  • Strong communication skills; able to represent the team upwards and translate business goals into clear technical scope and delivery plans.

  • Experience improving developer experience, CI/CD, release practices and delivery cadence across a team.

  • Confident using AI development tools every day, with experience of helping a team adopt them without letting quality slip.

PREFERABLE

descriptionHtml:
L’histoire du groupe Theodo et son succès
Theodo accompagne depuis 2009 les entreprises innovantes dans la conception, le développement et le déploiement de produits digitaux ingénieux - tels que la plateforme TF1+, l'application LCL Pro ou l'application France Identité Numérique - en tirant parti du meilleur de la technologie et de l’approche Lean.

Theodo connait une croissance exceptionnelle depuis 15 ans : nos équipes rassemblent plus de 750 Theodoers, principalement des Software Engineers, passionnés de technologie et d’amélioration continue. En 2025, le groupe Theodo génère 100M€ de CA. Chez Theodo HealthTech, l'entité experte en santé, nous accompagnons tous les acteurs de la santé dans le développement des dispositifs médicaux digitaux sur-mesure. Grâce à notre expérience du Lean et de la tech, combinées à notre connaissance de la santé, nous concevons et développons des dispositifs médicaux numériques qui s'intègrent dans le parcours de soins des patients (thérapies digitales - DTx, essais cliniques virtualisés, parcours de soins digitalisés). Notre but est de réaliser des produits qui changent la vie de leurs utilisateurs, qu'ils soient soignants ou patients.
Ton équipe : Chez Theodo, les techs travaillent en équipes projet, constituées en fonction des besoins de chaque client, réunissant Software Engineers, Tech Lead et Product Manager. Ensemble, ils collaborent étroitement avec le client, avec des échanges réguliers pour partager vos avancées, approfondir la compréhension de son problème et faire évoluer le produit au plus près des besoins de ses utilisateurs. En tant qu’Engineering Manager, ton rôle est de manager jusqu’à 4 tech leads, soit de chapeauter la réussite de 4 projets, en binôme avec un(e) Group Project Manager. Tes futures missions : Le besoin actuel porte sur des missions “grands-comptes” avec des produits et architectures complexes, développées par plusieurs squads de Theodo : - Manager & faire progresser les Tech Leads : tu accompagnes 1 à 4 Tech Leads dans leur montée en compétence et leur épanouissement. - Assurer le delivery technique : tu garantis la qualité du code (3S : stabilité, sécurité, vitesse), la tenue des jalons et la robustesse de l’architecture. - Contribuer au développement business : tu participes aux discussions stratégiques avec nos clients (DSI, sponsors…), tu aides à identifier des opportunités et tu es acteur de l’avant-vente avec nos sales. Les problématiques et les technos sont très différentes d’un projet à l’autre, voici quelques exemples : - Hub Santé : lancé par l’Agence du Numérique en Santé en 2024, vise à connecter en temps réel les 83 SAMU, SMUR, SDIS et autres acteurs de l’urgence, dans un écosystème historiquement fragmenté. Accompagnée par une équipe de 3 experts Theodo, l’ANS a déployé une plateforme nationale d’interopérabilité permettant une coordination critique plus fluide et sécurisée. Résultats : +10 SAMU connectés dès la phase pilote, interopérabilité effective sur plusieurs périmètres et conformité HDS maintenue. - Vidal : référence centenaire de l’information médicale, a développé avec Theodo un assistant médical basé sur l’IA générative pour fournir aux professionnels de santé des réponses fiables en un temps record et sécuriser la prescription. En 8 semaines, une équipe de 4 experts Theodo a conçu un POC de chatbot RAG connecté à la base Vidal, capable de réduire le temps de recherche tout en garantissant traçabilité et fiabilité des sources. Objectif : renforcer la confiance des praticiens et faire entrer Vidal dans l’ère du service médical “fonctionnel”. Tes perspectives d’évolutions : Perspectives d’évolution moyen terme (1 - 2 ans) : - Manageriale : VP Tech ou Group Manager - Technique : Architecte senior - Business/Influence : Thought Leader (animer une communauté tech) ou Intrapreneur (porter une nouvelle offre) Une méthodologie basée sur l’apprentissage continu : Chez Theodo, nous avons construit notre approche tech autour d’une conviction forte : on développe d’abord les personnes, avant de développer les produits. Notre Lean Tech® System met l’accent sur l’apprentissage continu : tu évolueras dans un environnement qui investit sur le long terme, où l’objectif est de te permettre de progresser chaque jour, tout en construisant des produits utiles et performants pour nos clients. Profil recherché : - 7 à 14 ans d’expérience professionnelle, avec une expérience confirmée en management d’équipes tech et en environnement ESN / conseil. - Basé(e) en région parisienne, avec une préférence pour une présence majoritaire au bureau, attendue pour un rôle stratégique et managérial. Hard skills - Solide expertise technologique (Java / Spring Boot et/ou Angular) permettant d’être crédible et légitime auprès des équipes, sans être attendu·e sur le code au quotidien. - Capacité à concevoir des architectures évolutives et à arbitrer des choix techniques dans des contextes grands comptes complexes. - Expérience significative en management d’équipes techniques, avec la capacité à débloquer des Tech - Leads sur des problématiques techniques complexes. - Capacité d’analyse et de résolution de problèmes complexes, avec un impact transverse dans l’organisation. - Intérêt pour l’IA générative et son usage dans la conception et le développement de produits digitaux. Soft skills - Leadership affirmé et posture pédagogique pour embarquer, inspirer et faire progresser des équipes exigeantes. - Orientation marquée business et création de valeur : chez Theodo, nous ne faisons pas de la tech pour la tech. - Aisance relationnelle et communicationnelle, avec la capacité d’adresser tous niveaux d’interlocuteurs, y compris C-level, et de mener des conversations exigeantes. Le process de recrutement : - Call de qualification (30 min) avec un membre de l’équipe recrutement - Cultural fit (1h) avec le même recruteur - Test technique de refactoring (à la maison + débrief 1h) - Entretien modélisation (1h) - Simulation vente d’architecture à un DSI (1h) - Final avec un dirigeant - Prise de référencePourquoi rejoindre Theodo HealthTech ? title: Engineering Manager - Compilers
descriptionHtml:
About Fractile

Fractile was founded in 2022 on the bet that, eventually, the world’s most capable AI systems would be limited in their impact by the time taken to produce useful outputs. We bet everything on the logical conclusion: that the only way to truly unlock this latent value, to make speed viable at scale, was to radically re-invent the hardware that we run our frontier AI models on. Ever since, we have been building chips and systems that tackle this problem: how to efficiently generate output at thousands of tokens per second, while handling the complexity and capacity challenges of operating large models at very long contexts.

 

The workloads that push to the limits of the current frontier are already transformational; it is the technical and economic limits on inference speed that are constraining progress. The defining work of the 21st century will be marked by the engine of inference delivering immense and diffuse chains of intellectual inquiry, in drug discovery, in software engineering, in materials discovery, in any field where progress is driven by deep reasoning and intelligence to resolve complex problems.

The role

Fractile is building a full-stack AI accelerator from the ground up, and the compiler team sits at the heart of how we deliver performance. As the Engineering Manager for Compilers, you will build and lead a team of 10+ engineers developing the compiler stack for our novel AI acceleration hardware, with direct responsibility for enabling industry-leading LLM inference performance on Fractile's accelerators. This is a hands-on technical leadership role in a fast-moving, collaborative environment where the compiler team works closely with hardware, driver, runtime and ML engineers across the stack. If you want to shape the architecture of a compiler from first principles, build a world-class team around it, and have your work directly determine the performance of next-generation AI hardware, this is the role.

What we’re looking for:

  • Proven track record of leadership experience managing a high-performance development team and delivering consistently outstanding outcomes.

  • Proven experience in compiler development, with experience of machine learning compilers and industry standard technologies such as MLIR or TVM being a significant advantage.

  • Up-to-date knowledge of machine learning techniques and technologies

  • A good understanding of computer architecture and performance optimisation techniques.

  • Excellent C/C++ skills and solid experience of industry standard development tools and technologies.

  • A creative and innovative mindset, and a willingness to take ownership and drive results in a fast-paced environment.

What you’re signing up for:

This is a young company doing hard things, at the intersection of novel silicon and the software stack that makes it useful. You'll be building and leading a compiler team as the hardware it targets is still taking shape, which means making architectural decisions against a specification first, then a simulator, then early silicon. The IR design, the lowering strategy, the execution model: you'll help define all of it before you can run it on real hardware. That takes comfort with ambiguity and the ability to make good calls with incomplete information. If that sounds frustrating, this probably isn't the role. If that sounds like the interesting part, we should talk.

The boundaries here are soft by design. The compiler team works closely with hardware architects, kernel engineers, runtime teams and ML researchers. You'll need to understand enough of what sits above and below your layer to make good decisions at the boundary, and to build a team that can do the same. That breadth is a feature of the job, not a distraction from it.

You'll be there when the first model runs end to end on Fractile silicon. When the lowering strategy you helped design produces a result the hardware team didn't think was possible yet. When the team you hired and grew ships something that goes into every rack we sell.

We want a team that reflects the world it's building for, and we welcome applicants from every background, including those whose path here hasn't been straight. We care that you're energised by this kind of work, that you build and develop great engineers, and that you make the people around you better.

Come build it with us.

What We Offer

  • Competitive salary: A competitive salary reflective of your experience and the specialist nature of the role.

  • Equity & Ownership: meaningful equity so everyone shares in the value creation

  • Benefits: Private Medical, Dental and Vision, Contributory Pension, 25 Days holiday plus bank holidays and Life/Critical Illness Insurance.

  • Diverse & fun office: we believe the hardest problems get solved by the broadest range of minds. We are committed to Equal Employment Opportunity through attracting and retaining a diverse team and building an inclusive environment.

Fractile is seeking to increase the clock speed of global progress, one chip at a time. We’ve recently raised $220M from investors including Founders Fund and Accel and our most important work lies ahead. Join us!

 

Export controls

Our work involves technologies subject to UK, US and other international export control regulations. Certain roles may require additional eligibility checks to ensure compliance with applicable law. We'll be transparent about this throughout the hiring process.

Trusted by thousands of businesses across more than 100 countries, Lokalise empowers millions of people worldwide to use digital services in their native languages. Backed by a customer-loved support team, our platform fits seamlessly into your design, development, and content workflows, helping you scale with consistency and control.

Location

While our company operates exclusively on a remote basis, you must reside and have the legal right to work in one of the following countries: the United Kingdom, Latvia, or Spain.

This is a full-time, remote position. Please note that we do not engage on a B2B or contractor basis.

About the Team

We're looking for an Engineering Manager to lead a cross-functional team in our Product Engineering organization. Each of our engineering teams owns a product domain at Lokalise, from vision to delivery. Teams talk to customers, find out what they need, set their own goals and choose how to solve the problems that matter most.

AI is already part of how we build software at Lokalise, and it's changing what great engineering leadership looks like. We're looking for a leader who stays close to the work and understands how AI is changing speed, quality and engineers' day-to-day experience. You'll keep your teams focused on outcomes that matter to our customers and our business, not just on how much gets shipped.

For this role, you'll lead our Editing Experience team. The team owns the tools linguists and reviewers use every day to translate, review and approve content at scale: the translation editor, the review and approval workflow, content management tools and the developer utilities that support them. Together with your Product Manager and Designer, you'll own the team's strategy and delivery end to end.

What You Will Do

  • Lead, coach and develop your teams of Software Engineers. You'll support their career growth, run performance evaluations, contribute to compensation planning and hire engineers who raise the bar.
  • Stay technically close to the work without becoming a bottleneck. You'll review key designs and pull requests, pair with engineers on tricky problems and take on contributions outside the critical path (such as tooling, prototypes or small fixes). This keeps you in touch with the codebase and your teams' daily reality while they own delivery.
  • Partner with Product Managers and Designers (the Product Triad) to understand our customers deeply and take part in discovery. You'll make sure your teams work on the right problems, putting outcomes ahead of outputs.
  • Connect engineering decisions to business impact. Understand how your domain contributes to customer value, retention and revenue, and use that to guide trade-offs on scope, investment and technical debt.
  • Own your teams' flow of work from start to finish. Track and act on delivery and quality signals (such as cycle time, deployment frequency, change failure rate and recovery time), clear bottlenecks across planning, review, testing and release, and keep cognitive load sustainable.
  • Lead your teams' move to AI-native engineering across the SDLC. Embed AI tools and agentic workflows, measure their real effect on speed, quality and how engineers experience their work, and adapt team practices so faster delivery never costs reliability or maintainability.
  • Champion operational excellence. Drive reliability and quality practices, own the health of the services your teams run and step in as Incident Commander when needed.
  • Own your teams' delivery: set quarterly plans, track progress against the product roadmap and help shape department-wide planning and strategy.

What You Must Have

  • 3+ years of recent experience as an Engineering Manager leading software engineering teams, ideally in SaaS product companies.
  • A strong software engineering background, and you're still hands-on today. You can review code and designs credibly, dig into technical issues and contribute to architecture decisions.
  • Proven people leadership: hiring, onboarding, coaching, performance management and helping engineers grow into their next role.
  • A strong product engineering mindset. You've partnered with Product and Design on discovery, worked directly with customers and measured success by customer and business outcomes rather than output.
  • Business acumen. You understand the commercial context, can explain trade-offs in terms of impact and communicate clearly with stakeholders at all levels.
  • Experience using engineering metrics and flow practices (such as DORA metrics, cycle time or WIP limits) to find bottlenecks and improve delivery, quality and team health, without turning metrics into targets.
  • Hands-on experience using AI-assisted development and agentic tools, both in your own work and across a team. You have a clear view of how AI changes delivery speed, code quality, review practices and cognitive load.
  • Experience planning and delivering complex initiatives across several teams predictably, including managing dependencies, risks and incidents.

It's a Plus If You Have

None of these are required, and we're happy to support you as you learn them on the job.

  • Experience in the localization industry or with translation workflows.
  • Experience leading engineering teams at a product company during a scale-up phase.
  • Experience shipping AI-powered product features, such as LLM-based features, to customers.
  • Experience managing fully remote, distributed teams.
  • Familiarity with developer experience or productivity frameworks, such as SPACE or DevEx.

Our Benefits

🌍 Fully remote setup with flexible working hours.
🏢 Co-working budget — for those days you want a change from your home office.
🌴 Flexible vacation policy to recharge when you need to.

📚 Learning & development budget to grow your skills and career.
🏥 Health insurance to keep you covered.
🧘 Wellness allowance to support your mental and physical well-being.
🤝 Great startup culture — remote but close-knit, with regular retreats and social events to stay connected.

Therefore, we welcome applications from people of all gender identities, sexual orientations, personal expressions, relationship, marital, or civil partnership statuses, racial identities, national or ethnic origins, religious beliefs, ages, and disability statuses.
