title: Forward Deployed Engineer, DACH
descriptionHtml:
About Telnyx

Telnyx is an industry leader that's not just imagining the future of global connectivity—we're building it. From architecting and amplifying the reach of a private, global, multi-cloud IP network, to bringing hyperlocal edge technology right to your fingertips through intuitive APIs, we're shaping a new era of seamless interconnection between people, devices, and applications.

We're driven by a desire to transform and modernize what's antiquated, automate the manual, and solve real-world problems through innovative connectivity solutions. As a testament to our success, we're proud to stand as a financially stable and profitable company. Our robust profitability allows us not only to invest in pioneering technologies but also to foster an environment of continuous learning and growth for our team.

Our collective vision is a world where borderless connectivity fuels limitless innovation. By joining us, you can be part of laying the foundations for this interconnected future. We're currently seeking passionate individuals who are excited about the opportunity to contribute to an industry-shaping company while growing their own skills and careers.

The Role

We're building a local Enterprise Sales Pod in Munich — one AE and one Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE), working together to build a Telnyx enterprise business in your market. You'll embed directly with enterprise customers to architect and ship production systems on Telnyx's global network — voice, messaging, AI, and wireless.

This isn't about demoing products. It's about building real solutions that work at scale.

You'll work side-by-side with a dedicated Enterprise AE — not a demo resource, but a commercial partner who owns the named-account list, builds executive relationships, and closes the deal. You own the technical side: discovery, architecture, POC, and production go-live. You win together. No throw-over-the-wall.

The Pod Model

Enterprise AE — owns the named-account list, builds executive relationships, gets in the room, owns commercial qualification and close, expands the account. .

Forward Deployed Engineer — owns technical discovery, designs the architecture, builds the POC when gated, gets the first workload live, removes blockers and finds the next workload.

We sell the workload, not the SKU. Customers buy a production outcome — an AI contact center, a SOC/NOC agent, global communications, connected mobility, or enterprise inference — that runs on Telnyx primitives (voice, messaging, numbers, wireless, Voice AI, inference, agents, connectivity). You lead with the outcome conversation, not a product menu.

What You'll Do

• Embed with enterprise customers to understand their communications workflows, AI use cases, and integration challenges firsthand
• Build and deploy custom implementations: AI Voice Assistants, Telnyx APIs (Voice, Messaging, Fax, Wireless), WebRTC
• Run open-weight LLMs in customer environments — consume GLM, Kimi, DeepSeek, Qwen, and MiniMax through Telnyx Inference (OpenAI-compatible API; there's no model infrastructure for you to run), or deploy self-hosted stacks (Llama, Mistral, and region-specific models like Aleph Alpha's Luminous, or sovereign EU models) behind your own serving engine when air-gapped or sovereign-cloud requirements demand it
• Deploy and operate LiteLLM as the model gateway in customer environments: a unified OpenAI-compatible interface across self-hosted open-weight models and hosted providers, with routing, load balancing, retries and fallbacks, rate limits, and per-team virtual keys
• Instrument and govern LLM usage through the gateway — cost tracking and budgets, caching, logging and observability (OpenTelemetry, Langfuse, or similar), and guardrails — so customers can see and control what their AI workloads are doing
• Wire production observability for everything you ship — metrics, logs, traces, dashboards, and alerting (e.g. Prometheus + Grafana for metrics, OpenTelemetry for traces, Graylog or ELK for logs — or the customer's existing stack) — so you and the customer's ops team both know what "healthy" looks like and what pages whom when it isn't
• Design model routing strategies for real-time voice workloads, balancing latency, cost, and quality, with sane fallback behavior when a provider degrades
• Make the build-vs-buy case between self-hosted open-weight models and hosted frontier APIs, and keep the customer's application code portable across both
• Adapt models to customer domains: prompt and RAG pipelines and evaluation harnesses for German-language use cases and DACH-specific regulatory environments (GDPR, EU AI Act, German data localization)
• Lead POCs, pilots, and production launches from whiteboard to go-live
• Own customer outcomes — stay engaged until the solution is live and stable
• Collaborate directly with Product and Engineering to shape the roadmap based on field insights from Germany, Austria, and Switzerland
• Create clear technical documentation, runbooks, and maintainable solutions for handoff • Troubleshoot and resolve complex integration issues alongside customer teams

What We're Looking For

• CS degree or equivalent experience
• 3+ years building and shipping production software — you've written code that real users depended on, you've been on-call for it, and you've debugged it when things broke. (A consulting background counts if this is also true of you.)
• Proficiency in multiple languages: Python, Node.js/TypeScript, Go — you're more dangerous in some than others. (Telnyx Edge Compute — functions and stateful actors — is TypeScript, so that one pulls double duty.)
• Practical understanding of what breaks in front of a model in production: provider rate limits and quotas, timeout and retry behavior, streaming, token accounting and cost attribution, and the failure modes that only show up under concurrency
• Comfortable deploying containerized services on Kubernetes, with secrets management, config, and upgrades as part of the deployment story
• You've wired observability and been paged because of it — Prometheus + Grafana, OpenTelemetry, Graylog, ELK, or equivalent. You know what to monitor, what to alert on, and what "healthy" looks like
• High-concurrency experience — Kafka, message queues, or event streams at real scale. When throughput spikes you know what breaks — consumer lag, backpressure, hot partitions, rebalance stalls — and what absorbs it: partitioning, consumer groups, parallelism up to your partition count
• You've built APIs from scratch, not just consumed them — OpenAPI spec, REST/GraphQL design, auth, rate limiting, versioning, idempotency
• Event-driven thinking and cloud-native instincts
• Exposure to SIP, WebRTC, or real-time voice/messaging systems
• Self-sufficient by default — there's no engineering team behind you. You read the code and the docs, ask the customer (not your manager), and make sound engineering judgment calls on your own
• Customer-facing engineering experience — you can run discovery with a customer's engineers and present to their executives in the same week
• Ability to translate "it's not working" into root cause
• Comfortable working on customer sites and in high-stakes technical conversations
• Excellent written and verbal communication in English and German. You can run whiteboard sessions, live troubleshooting, and escalations with customer engineering teams.
• Based in Munich, or willing to relocate — this is a hybrid role with travel across Germany, Austria, and Switzerland
• Legally authorized to work in Germany, or eligible for sponsorship

Bonus Points For

• Experience with AI voice assistants, STT/TTS, or LLM-based conversational systems
• Building eval sets for a specific domain
• Hands-on production experience with an LLM gateway — LiteLLM, Portkey, Kong AI Gateway, or an in-house OpenAI-compatible proxy — including config-driven model definitions, routing and fallback rules, and virtual key management
• Familiarity with the open-weight model landscape and the trade-offs between regional and multilingual models, including EU sovereign AI initiatives (Gaia-X, Aleph Alpha, European LLM projects)
• Experience with an inference serving engine behind the gateway — vLLM, SGLang, or TGI for production serving; Ollama for lightweight on-prem — and sizing GPU capacity for self-hosted models (KV-cache footprint, concurrent batch size, and context length against VRAM)
• SQL proficiency (Postgres, MySQL, Oracle)
• ETL and data wrangling experience
• CI/CD pipeline design and automation
• Background in telecom, CPaaS, or high-growth SaaS
• Experience with sovereign or on-prem cloud deployments and DACH regulatory frameworks (GDPR, EU AI Act, German data sovereignty and localization requirements, Swiss data protection)
• Security mindset (IAM, encryption, audit logging)

descriptionHtml:
About HappyRobot

HappyRobot is the infrastructure for enterprises to build and orchestrate AI workforces. Our AI workers don't just communicate through voice and email - they make decisions, take action, and run operations autonomously across entire enterprise systems. Born in Y Combinator (S23) and backed by a16z, Base10, Prysm Capital and Eurazeo with over $150M raised, we power critical operations for global enterprises worldwide.

Our platform is battle-tested in the most demanding environments, where AI has real consequences. We started in logistics, built our own voice stack, models, and orchestration layer from the ground up, and are now bringing that infrastructure to every enterprise that runs the real economy. Learn more about our vision in our manifesto.

Role Overview

We are looking for a versatile and highly skilled German-speaking Forward Deployed Engineer to join our team. In this role, you will combine strong technical abilities with excellent communication skills, working directly with customers to ensure they maximize the value of HappyRobot’s AI platform. You will be involved in onboarding, implementation, and ongoing support, while also contributing to product development and innovation.


At HappyRobot, there’s no role seniority or hierarchy — we operate as a team of builders. We execute, we build, we own, and we care deeply about our customers and their success.

What You’ll Do

  • Customer-Facing Engineering – Work closely with customers from onboarding to ongoing usage, helping them integrate and optimize our AI solutions.

  • Technical Development – Build new features, MVPs, and scalable solutions that directly impact customer outcomes.

  • Full-Stack Development – Utilize React, TypeScript, Node.js, and Python to develop robust applications and tools.

  • AI/ML Applications – Design, implement, and iterate on AI/ML solutions, including LLM prompting, tuning of voices, and transcribers to optimize use cases.

  • Integration & APIs – Manage APIs and integrations with third-party systems to ensure seamless functionality for customers.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration – Partner with Product, Engineering, and Customer Success teams to deliver tailored solutions.

  • Iterative Problem-Solving – Continuously iterate and improve AI solutions based on customer feedback and evolving requirements.

  • Project Management – Prioritize and manage multiple projects under tight deadlines while maintaining high-quality results.

Must Have

  • Strong full-stack experience: React, TypeScript, Node.js.

  • Hands-on proficiency in Python.

  • Experience building AI/ML applications, including LLM prompting and tuning.

  • Ability to manage APIs and integrate with third-party systems.

  • Excellent communication skills with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders.

  • Proven ability to prioritize and manage multiple projects under tight deadlines.

  • Founder mindset: highly independent, takes ownership, and thrives in a fast-paced environment.

Why join us?

  • Join a world-class team of engineers and builders.

  • Backed by top investors including a16z, Y Combinator, Base10, Prysm Capital and Eurazeo.

  • Have ownership and autonomy of projects and are encouraged to ship.

  • Comprehensive Benefits including healthcare, dental, vision coverage.

  • Competitive salary + equity in a high-growth startup.

Our Operating Principles

Extreme Ownership

We take full responsibility for our work, outcomes, and team success. No excuses, no blame-shifting — if something needs fixing, we own it and make it better. This means stepping up, even when it’s not “your job.” If a ball is dropped, we pick it up. If a customer is unhappy, we fix it. If a process is broken, we redesign it. We don’t wait for someone else to solve it — we lead with accountability and expect the same from those around us.

Craftsmanship

Putting care and intention into every task, striving for excellence, and taking deep ownership of the quality and outcome of your work. Craftsmanship means never settling for “just fine.” We sweat the details because details compound. Whether it’s a product feature, an internal doc, or a sales call — we treat it as a reflection of our standards. We aim to deliver jaw-dropping customer experiences by being curious, meticulous, and proud of what we build — even when nobody’s watching.

We are “majos”
Be friendly & have fun with your coworkers. Always be genuine & honest, but kind. “Majo” is our way of saying: be a good human. Be approachable, helpful, and warm. We’re building something ambitious, and it’s easier (and more fun) when we enjoy the ride together. We give feedback with kindness, challenge each other with respect, and celebrate wins together without ego.

Urgency with Focus
Create the highest impact in the shortest amount of time. Move fast, but in the right direction. We operate with speed because time is our most limited resource. But speed without focus is chaos. We prioritize ruthlessly, act decisively, and stay aligned. We aim for high leverage: the biggest results from the simplest, smartest actions. We’re running a high-speed marathon — not a sprint with no strategy.

Talent Density and Meritocracy
Hire only people who can raise the average; ‘exceptional performance is the passing grade.’ Ability trumps seniority. We believe the best teams are built on talent density — every hire should raise the bar. We reward contribution, not titles or tenure. We give ownership to those who earn it, and we all hold each other to a high standard. A-players want to work with other A-players — that’s how we win.

First-Principles Thinking
Strip a problem to physics-level facts, ignore industry dogma, rebuild the solution from scratch. We don’t copy-paste solutions. We go back to basics, ask why things are the way they are, and rebuild from the ground up if needed. This mindset pushes us to innovate, challenge stale assumptions, and move faster than incumbents. It’s how we build what others think is impossible.

descriptionHtml:
Founders Bay ist ein equity-free Accelerator für Startups im ländlichen Raum und für den Mittelstand.

Gerade bauen wir das Geschäft mit Unternehmen und Partnern stark aus. Mittelständler und Corporates sollen mit uns passende Startups finden und Piloten aufsetzen. Banken, Stiftungen und Verbände sollen unsere Programme mittragen. Genau dafür suchen wir Verstärkung.

Wir suchen ab sofort eine Founder Associate (w/m/d) für unsere Weiterentwicklung. Du willst Startups und Unternehmen zusammenbringen, führst gern selbst Gespräche und löst Probleme lieber mit einem selbst gebauten KI-Workflow als mit einer Excel-Liste? Dann lies weiter.

Wir machen nicht nur automatisierte Kaltakquise. Wir wollen, dass Unternehmen von sich aus zu uns kommen, über unser Scouting-Tool foundersbay.ventures, über Fachmedien, Partner und auch über die Antworten von ChatGPT und Co. Daran baust du mit.

Qualifikation

title: Founder's Associate Intern
descriptionHtml:
Als Founders Associate Intern arbeitest du direkt an der Seite des Founding Teams und bist in die wichtigsten strategischen und operativen Themen eingebunden. Du entwickelst neue Ideen und Geschäftsansätze mit und bringst sie hands-on in die Umsetzung. Dabei übernimmst du von Anfang an Verantwortung, treibst eigene Projekte voran und sorgst dafür, dass aus Ideen konkrete Ergebnisse werden. Neben Business Development und Business Operations bist du auch im Daily Business eng eingebunden und koordinierst wichtige Schnittstellen zu Investoren, Banken und weiteren Stakeholdern.

Wir suchen bewusst keine klassische Praktikantin bzw. keinen klassischen Praktikanten, sondern jemanden mit Entrepreneurial Mindset und echtem Drive, der Lust hat, ein Unternehmen von Anfang an mit aufzubauen. Die Rolle ist dabei mehr als ein Praktikum: Unser Ziel ist es, die Person im Anschluss idealerweise als ersten Full-Time Hire langfristig ins Team zu holen.

Worum es geht

Die Energiewende braucht Kapital. Gleichzeitig wächst in Deutschland der Markt für Erneuerbare-Energie-Projekte – doch die passende Finanzierung kommt noch viel zu selten effizient zustande. Was bislang fehlt, ist ein Tech-Layer, der Investoren, Projektentwickler und Banken intelligent miteinander verbindet.

Wir glauben, dass darin enormes Potenzial steckt. Deshalb arbeiten wir aktuell im Stealth Mode an einer neuen Lösung, die genau hier ansetzt. Dafür suchen wir Menschen, die Lust haben, von Anfang an Verantwortung zu übernehmen, eigene Ideen einzubringen und die Entwicklung aktiv mitzugestalten. Mehr über unsere Vision und das, woran wir arbeiten, erzählen wir dir gerne im persönlichen Gespräch.

Was du in den 6 Monaten machst

Ein großer Teil deiner Arbeit besteht darin, das Tagesgeschäft am Laufen zu halten, Themen eigenständig voranzutreiben und dafür zu sorgen, dass wir als Unternehmen immer schneller werden. Gleichzeitig arbeitest du eng mit dem Founding Team an strategischen Fragestellungen und entwickelst die Hypothesen mit, die unsere Richtung und unser Wachstum bestimmen.

  • Operations: Du steuerst den Prozess mit Investoren von der ersten Anfrage bis zum Finanzierungsabschluss. Dabei koordinierst du die dazugehörigen Prozesse und entwickelst unsere operativen Abläufe weiter.

  • Strategie: Gemeinsam mit dem Founding Team entwickelst du unsere Unternehmensstrategie weiter und baust das Finanzmodell auf, mit dem wir unser Wachstum planen und steuern.

  • AI und Automatisierung: Du baust mit AI und No-Code-Tools, automatisierst Prozesse und bringst unsere Plattform auf das nächste Level.

  • Go-to-Market: Du arbeitest aktiv an unserem Markteintritt mit, identifizierst potenzielle Partner und baust Beziehungen zu Banken und anderen Finanzierern auf.

Was du mitbringst

  • Idealerweise hast du deinen Bachelor oder Master abgeschlossen oder bist kurz vor dem Abschluss. Das ist aber keine zwingende Voraussetzung.

  • Erste Praktika in Start-ups, Beratung oder Venture Capital.

  • Erfahrung in Finance oder im Bereich erneuerbare Energien ist ein Plus.

  • Du denkst unternehmerisch, erkennst Probleme und wartest nicht darauf, dass dir jemand die Lösung vorgibt.

  • Du arbeitest täglich mit AI-Tools und setzt neue Tools direkt in deiner Arbeit ein.

  • Du triffst Entscheidungen auch dann, wenn nicht alle Informationen vorliegen, und stehst für das Ergebnis ein.

  • Die Energiewende interessiert dich.

  • Fließendes Deutsch und Englisch

Eher nicht passend, wenn ...

  • du suchst ein klassisches Praktikum mit klar abgegrenzten Aufgaben und festen Routinen.

  • du fühlst dich wohler mit klaren Vorgaben, statt eigene Lösungen zu entwickeln.

  • du lieber auf Freigaben wartest, als selbst anzufangen.

  • dich Rückschläge schnell aus der Bahn werfen. In einem frühen Unternehmen läuft vieles nicht beim ersten Mal, und Probleme landen oft ungefiltert auf dem Tisch.

  • du den ganzen Tag nur an der großen Strategie feilen willst. Der Alltag in der Early Stage besteht zum Großteil aus Umsetzung, auch bei den Gründern.

Was wir bieten

  • Option auf Übernahme nach den 6 Monaten

  • Mitgliedschaft im Urban Sports Club

  • Du bist bei den wichtigen Entscheidungen dabei, auch in Bank- und Investorengesprächen.

  • Eigene Projekte, für die du verantwortlich bist und deren Ergebnis du direkt siehst

  • Eine steile Lernkurve an der Schnittstelle von Finance, Energie und AI

title: Founding EMEA Account Executive - German-Speaking  (Switzerland)
descriptionHtml:
About Pallet

Pallet is building AI Agents to transform the physical economy, a $12 trillion global TAM. We’ve raised $50M from top investors, including General Catalyst, Bessemer Venture Partners, and Bain Capital Ventures. 

Our mission is to increase the efficiency of the global supply chain by automating the manual workflows that slow supply chain teams down. Our flagship platform provides end-to-end visibility, and control.

As companies across the physical economy look to drive efficiency, many are turning to Pallet to lead the way. With deep supply chain expertise and cutting-edge AI capabilities, we’re positioned to build the next $10B company powering the physical economy.

Join us and work alongside leaders from Google, DoorDash, YC, and more to shape the future of supply chain technology.

Remote from Switzerland

You could be an Enterprise Account Executive anywhere. Why us?

  • Join a well-funded, high-growth startup on a clear path to $100M ARR.
  • Sell a category-defining AI Agents platform with massive surface area across logistics.
  • Build Pallet’s presence across Europe as one of the first commercial hires on the ground.
  • Work directly with founders and senior leadership to define our international go-to-market strategy.
  • Help transform one of the world’s largest industries while building toward a $10B+ outcome.

About the opportunity

We’re hiring our first Founding Enterprise Account Executives in EMEA to build Pallet’s commercial presence across Europe.

You’ll own net-new enterprise acquisition across the region, build relationships with the largest logistics providers in Europe, and help establish the playbook for our international expansion. This is a highly consultative enterprise sales role focused on educating customers on an entirely new category of AI-powered workflow automation.

You’ll partner closely with Sales, Product, Engineering, Solutions, and Customer Success to drive a solution-selling motion centered around workflow discovery, AI use case identification, structured pilots, and measurable ROI.

This role will be remote from Switzerland. 

How you will make an impact

  • Own the full enterprise sales cycle across EMEA, from outbound prospecting through contract signature.
  • Build and maintain a 3x-4x qualified pipeline through disciplined outbound execution while self-sourcing at least 30% of opportunities.
  • Develop relationships with executive stakeholders across Europe’s largest logistics providers, including COO, CIO, VP Operations, VP Supply Chain, and VP Technology.
  • Lead consultative discovery sessions that map operational workflows to Pallet’s AI agent capabilities.
  • Scope and lead structured pilots that demonstrate measurable operational ROI and convert into enterprise deployments.
  • Build executive business cases that align operational improvements with financial outcomes.
  • Document repeatable customer use cases and market feedback to shape Pallet’s product roadmap and international GTM strategy.
  • Help establish Pallet as the leading AI platform for enterprise logistics across Europe.

What we’re looking for

  • 8+ years of enterprise B2B SaaS or enterprise logistics sales experience.
  • Business-fluent German: you can run discovery, negotiate and present to executives in German. 
  • Proven track record of consistently closing six- and seven-figure enterprise software agreements.
  • Strong consultative selling and value-based sales methodology.
  • Experience navigating complex buying committees and long enterprise sales cycles.
  • Executive presence with senior operators and technology leaders.
  • Comfortable selling technical, workflow-heavy software products.
  • Ability to quickly understand complex logistics operations and translate them into compelling AI automation opportunities.
  • Excellent outbound prospecting and territory-building discipline.
  • Willingness to travel extensively across Europe.

Experience selling into logistics, supply chain, transportation, or warehouse operations is strongly preferred but not required. Candidates without logistics experience should demonstrate an ability to quickly learn operational workflows and become trusted advisors to customers.

Working model

Working hours are generally 9:00am-6:00pm London time, providing full coverage of the European business day while maintaining regular collaboration with our San Francisco headquarters.

You’ll typically spend:

  • Mornings and early afternoons working directly with European customers and prospects.
  • Late afternoons collaborating with our US-based Sales, Product, and Engineering teams during our daily overlap window.
  • Approximately 65% of your time traveling across Europe for customer meetings, executive workshops, pilots, and industry events.

Reporting structure

You’ll report directly to our VP of Global Revenue, for territory strategy, customer relationships, and international expansion and will participate in weekly pipeline reviews, forecasting, and sales process alignment with the US team.

Interview Process

  • Chat with Christy - Business Recruiter - 30 mins
  • Deal Review - 30 mins
  • Discovery Mock Interview - 45-60 mins
  • Final Interview - ~2.5 hours
  • Brief Background Check and Reference Check

We move fast, and we’ll keep you informed at every stage of the process.

Compensation

The estimated compensation range for this role is 280-340k CHF OTE, 50/50 split, depending on experience and skill set.

Our compensation follows a standard 50/50 enterprise sales structure consisting of base salary and target commission. High performers are eligible for uncapped commission accelerators above quota.

In addition to cash compensation, we offer competitive equity, benefits, and significant growth opportunities as one of our earliest international commercial hires.

Final compensation will be determined based on experience, qualifications, and demonstrated enterprise sales performance.

Our Benefits 

We invest in our people the same way we invest in our product: seriously.

  • 🩺 Health, Vision, and Dental benefits 
  • 🏝️ Take-what-you-need Paid Vacation
  • ➕ Life Insurance and Accidental Insurance 
  • ❤️‍🩹 Short-Term Disability Coverage
  • 💸 Generous salary and equity for all staff
  • 🪜 401k option; helping you save for the future
  • 🧑‍🧑‍🧒‍🧒 Paid parental leave to support growing families
  • 📚 Yearly learning and development stipend
  • 🚌 Commuter benefits for Bay Area and New York employees
  • 🚘 Uber ride stipend if you ever have to work late in the office 
  • 🏡 Remote office home stipend to get you comfy in your space for remote employees
  •  📸 Free professional headshot 
  • 🍔 Daily catered lunches and dinners provided in office
  • 💪 Complimentary On-Site Gym: Our SF office has a fully equipped gym 
  • ✈️ Onboarding trip to one of our offices if you work remotely
  • 🥤 Monthly happy hours
  • 🎉 Annual Company Offsites; our last one was in Palm Springs CA 🌴

Workplace Policy

We are an in-person company. Our offices in San Francisco, New York City and London are where ideas get built, decisions get made, and the team gets stronger. We have invested in making them genuinely great places to spend your day, with catered lunches, monthly happy hours, and people who care about the work and each other.

Most of our team works in office five days a week. For select roles, we hire remotely across the U.S. Remote employees come to one of our offices for their first week to onboard and meet the team, and we cover the full trip. 

Every role is different. Travel expectations are always shared upfront in the job description and confirmed in your first call with us.

Equal Opportunity

We provide equal employment opportunities to all applicants and employees without discrimination on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, disability status, or any other applicable legally protected characteristic. title: Founding GTM Lead (Sales) (m/w/d)
descriptionHtml:
Über snipKI

snipKI bringt KI in den DACH-Mittelstand und in Konzerne: mit KI-Strategie und Roadmaps für das C-Level, Enablement-Programmen wie dem KI-Führerschein und dem KI Leadership Programm sowie der Implementierung erster Agentensysteme. Über 100 Programme und rund 3.500 befähigte Menschen, im Mittelstand ebenso wie in Konzernen.

Bisher verkaufen wir vor allem über die Gründer, Empfehlungen und Inbound. Das trägt, aber es skaliert nicht. Deshalb suchen wir die erste Person, die Vertrieb bei snipKI hauptberuflich verantwortet und den Go-to-Market mit uns aufbaut.

Deine Rolle

Als Founding GTM Lead verantwortest du den Neukundenvertrieb von snipKI von Ende zu Ende: vom Erstgespräch über Bedarfsanalyse und Angebot bis zur Unterschrift. Gleichzeitig baust du das Sales-System, auf dem später ein Team arbeitet. Du berichtest direkt an Moritz Heininger (Co-Founder und Geschäftsführer).

Deine Aufgaben

  • Neugeschäft abschließen: Du führst Discovery Calls mit Geschäftsführung, Abteilungs- und Fachbereichsleitungen sowie HR, erstellst Angebote im vereinbarten Preisrahmen und bringst Deals zum Abschluss.
  • Beratend verkaufen: Du verstehst, wo ein Unternehmen bei KI steht, und kombinierst daraus das passende Paket aus KI-Roadmap, KI Leadership Programm, KI-Führerschein, Workshops, Lernplattform und Implementierung.
  • Das Sales-System bauen: Playbook, Discovery-Leitfaden, Angebotslogik, Pipeline-Stages in HubSpot und ein wöchentlicher Forecast, auf den wir uns verlassen können.
  • Pipeline aufbauen: Inbound-Leads und Partnerleads qualifizieren, eigenes Netzwerk und Outbound nutzen, gemeinsam mit unserem GTM-Engineering-Team, das Listen, Enrichment und Sequenzen liefert.
  • Kunden ausbauen: Nach dem ersten Programm planst du mit deinen Kunden den nächsten Schritt, etwa weitere Teams, Führungskräfte oder eine Roadmap, gemeinsam mit unseren Trainer:innen und Consultants.
  • Team aufbauen: Wenn der Vertrieb wächst, kann frühestens nach 12 Monaten auch Führungsverantwortung für ein Sales-Team zu dir kommen.

Was nicht bei dir liegt

Damit du dich aufs Verkaufen konzentrieren kannst, übernehmen andere: die Durchführung der Programme (Trainer:innen und Education-Team), die operative Kundenbetreuung (Operations), CRM-Pflege, Recherche und Sequenz-Bau (GTM-Engineering) sowie Marketing, Brand und PR.

Was du mitbringst

  • Mehrere Jahre B2B-Vertrieb erklärungsbedürftiger Dienstleistungen, idealerweise Beratung, Weiterbildung oder SaaS, mit nachweisbaren Abschlüssen im fünf- bis sechsstelligen Bereich.
  • Erfahrung mit Buying Centern im Mittelstand und in Konzernen: Geschäftsführung, Abteilungs- und Fachbereichsleitungen, HR, Einkauf.
  • Echtes Interesse an KI. Du nutzt die Tools selbst und kannst mit Kund:innen auf Augenhöhe über ihre Situation sprechen.
  • Lust auf Aufbau: Du willst Prozesse schaffen, nicht nur abarbeiten, und arbeitest gern ohne fertige Strukturen.
  • Sicherer Umgang mit CRM (idealerweise HubSpot) und Freude an sauberen Zahlen.
  • Verhandlungssicheres Deutsch, gutes Englisch.
  • Bereitschaft, regelmäßig zu Kund:innen und ins Team nach Berlin zu reisen.

Was wir bieten

  • Vergütung: Attraktives Fixgehalt plus ungedeckelte Provision auf den Umsatz deiner Neukunden. Einfaches Modell, keine KPI-Matrix, monatliche Abrechnung nach Zahlungseingang. OTE im ersten Jahr rund 140.000 €.
  • Beteiligung: Möglichkeit, über unser Mitarbeiterbeteiligungsprogramm am Erfolg von snipKI teilzuhaben.
  • Gestaltungsraum: Du bist die erste Sales-Person und baust den Vertrieb mit den Gründern auf, mit direktem Draht und kurzen Wegen.
  • Ein Produkt, das gefragt ist: Inbound, Referenzkunden und eine starke Marke im DACH-Raum, du startest nicht bei null.
  • Arbeitsweise: Berlin oder remote innerhalb Deutschlands, Office und Kundentermine nach Bedarf, 2 bis 4 Team-Events pro Jahr im In- und Ausland, 30 Tage Urlaub.
  • Ausstattung ab Tag 1: MacBook, HubSpot, Clay, Lemlist, Call-Recording und Zugriff auf alle bisherigen Sales Calls. Dazu ein strukturiertes Onboarding, damit du schnell sicher in Produkten, Kunden und Pitch bist.
  • KI-Enablement aus erster Hand: Du arbeitest mit genau den Tools und Methoden, die wir unseren Kunden beibringen.
  • Firmenfitness: für alle Vollzeit-Mitarbeitenden.

Der Bewerbungsprozess

Kein Anschreiben. Schick uns stattdessen drei kurze Videos, eins pro Frage, jeweils maximal 5 Minuten. Mit dem Handy aufnehmen reicht völlig, uns geht es um dich und nicht um Filmproduktion:

  • Welcher Deal, den du abgeschlossen hast, macht dich am stolzesten, und warum?
  • Wie würdest du die ersten 90 Tage bei snipKI angehen?
  • Wofür nutzt du KI heute selbst?

Danach folgen ein erstes Kennenlernen mit Lina, eine Case Study und zum Abschluss ein Gespräch mit Jens und weiteren Leuten aus dem Team. So lernst du möglichst viele von uns kennen und bekommst ein echtes Bild davon, wie wir arbeiten. Start: idealerweise im Januar 2027.

title: Founding lead Product Designer
descriptionHtml:
Raison is on a mission to provide humans with better skills so they can feel confident and have more opportunities in the AI era. We help companies make sure 100% their teams master AI, directly in the flow of work (Teams, Slack) so that AI knowledge spreads across the organization instead of pooling in a handful of champions.

We are passionate entrepreneurs believing that the ongoing AI revolution should be shared by all employees; and that the future of corporate interactions should not be restricted to private human-machine chats. Raison is capturing what champions create with AI, turning it into shared, governed skills, and propagating them so everyone feels capable and empowered; acting as a powerful lever to accelerate the AI transformation of corporates.

We recently raised €2m from a top French VC + BPI and a selection of high-profile business angels who believe AI mastery is the highest-leverage application of AI inside companies.

Tasks

User Research & Discovery

  • Own field research: contextual inquiry, user interviews, and observation of how teams actually work with AI and where it breaks.
  • Build and maintain a deep understanding of our core users — individual contributors, champions, managers, and corporate buyers — and the context they operate in.
  • Synthesize messy field data into sharp, actionable insight: jobs-to-be-done, adoption blockers, and the conditions under which a skill transfers between people.
  • Establish a continuous discovery habit so research is a foundational reflex, and champion the user's perspective in every product decision.

Product & Experience Design

title: Freelance Senior Technical Advisor
descriptionHtml:
Role Details

Level: Senior/ Lead

Start Date: ASAP

Duration: 6 months

Day Rate: Dependent on experience

Weekly hours: 3-4 days/ week

Location: Remote Europe, GMT/BST or CET friendly

Language: English, plus Spanish and/or Portuguese

 

In this role, you’ll be a senior technical advisor to city governments across North, Central and South America, working in both an advisory and a hands-on capacity to help them design, build and launch small scale pilots of new services for residents.

Working alongside experienced product managers, data scientists, AI engineers, and designers, you’ll help multidisciplinary city teams build in-house product development capability by prototyping and delivering digital products and services, many of which harness data and AI.

You won’t own the decisions, but you’ll shape them. You’ll guide cities through the full product development lifecycle, helping them weigh the strategic and technical trade-offs at each stage: how to design system and data architecture that’s right-sized for a pilot but built to scale, how to prototype and test possible solutions to validate assumptions, and when AI approaches such as machine learning or large language models are the right tool (and when they aren’t). You’ll roll up your sleeves to prototype and demonstrate what good looks like, while making sure your clients understand the reasoning well enough to own the outcome.

This role suits someone with the technical depth of a tech lead, and the judgement, communication skills and patience to lead through influence rather than authority. You’ll need to work fluently in English and in at least one of Spanish or Portuguese.

 

Key skills and experiences

  • Extensive hands-on technical experience, with strong knowledge of system and data architecture, data pipelines, DevOps and infrastructure, and a track record of delivering and deploying robust solutions end to end, from prototype to pilot, across cloud, on-premises and hybrid environments, including legacy systems and resource-constrained ones, so that your recommendations are realistic and buildable.

  • Familiarity with AI and machine learning approaches, including large language models, and experience deploying them or working alongside ML engineers to integrate them into products, with enough understanding to judge when they’re the right tool and how to build them in responsibly.

  • Experience taking products from early concept to first release, while laying foundations for scale, with a track record of rapid prototyping and assumption testing and a “show, don’t tell” approach that uses working prototypes to build shared understanding and inform decisions.

  • Experience working in multidisciplinary teams, collaborating closely with product managers, designers and other disciplines throughout the product lifecycle.

  • The ability to explain technical ideas and trade-offs clearly to audiences of all technical levels, from engineers to non-technical stakeholders and senior decision-makers.

  • Experience setting technical direction for a project or small team and guiding other engineers, as a tech lead or senior engineer.

  • Experience influencing technical decisions you don't directly control, whether in a consulting or advisory role or as an in-house engineer working across teams and with senior stakeholders.

  • Curiosity and flexibility in problem solving, and comfort working through ambiguity and uncertainty in complex environments.

  • Professional working proficiency in English and in Spanish and/or Portuguese.

Nice to have

  • Experience working with multicultural teams and on international projects.

  • Experience working with government or other public-sector organisations, or on services for residents and citizens.

  • Familiarity with responsible AI practices, such as data privacy, bias and fairness, transparency, and the governance considerations specific to public-sector use of AI.

  • Experience supporting organisations to build their own technical capability, for example through coaching, mentoring or setting up new teams and practices.

Our hiring process

We’ve kept the process short and focused. Here’s what to expect:

1. Application & Video
As part of your application, we’ll ask you to record a short video (1–3 minutes, instructions below) describing a technical project — work or personal — that you really enjoyed working on.

  • Please record it in Spanish or Portuguese, whichever you speak fluently.

  • You don’t need to show your face — a voiceover on a screen share, or any other format you’re comfortable with, is fine.

  • We want to understand what the project was and why you enjoyed working on it. This isn’t a test of production quality; we’re interested in how you think and talk about your work.

2. Initial screening call
A short conversation to cover the basics — your timezone, working languages, availability, and a chance for you to ask early questions about the role and how we work.

3. Technical interview (~60 minutes)
A deeper conversation about your technical background and experience. We’ll talk through how you’ve approached real problems, the decisions you’ve made, and how you’d apply that thinking to the work at IF.

4. Ways of working interview (~45–60 minutes)
A conversation about how you collaborate, communicate, and work with others — including how you operate in an advisory capacity with clients and teams.

We’ll aim to keep you updated at every stage and let you know the outcome promptly after each step.


How to record and submit your video

The simplest way is Loom (free, no download needed):

  1. Go to loom.com and create a free account.

  2. Click New video → Record a video in your browser. Choose Screen and camera or Screen only if you’d prefer not to appear on camera, and make sure your microphone is selected.

  3. Record your video — remember, 1 to 3 minutes is all we need. The free plan has a 5-minute limit, which is plenty.

  4. When you stop recording, Loom will open the video and give you a link. Click Copy link.

  5. Check the sharing setting is Anyone with the link can view.

  6. Paste the link into the Link to your video field on the application form.

title: Go-To-Market Associate
descriptionHtml:

Hey there! We're Lleverage, and we're making the Autonomous Back Office actually achievable for businesses. We enable teams to capture, automate, and integrate AI agents into their business, because AI is only useful when it actually fits into daily operations.

We help the most strategic European industries – manufacturing, logistics, and wholesale – automate the messy, manual processes that most tools can’t handle.

We’re a fast-growing, VC-backed scale-up based in Amsterdam, with big ambitions for 2026 and beyond. This is your chance to join early, have real impact, and grow alongside the company. If that sounds something you want to help build, we'd love to have you on board!

About the role

We're looking for an exceptional Go-To-Market Associate who will be the engine of our commercial team. As part of the top 1% of Commercial talents globally, you'll combine systematic prospecting with creative outreach to build relationships with decision-makers who need AI solutions.

This is not a classic sales role. We're looking for a builder with a commercial brain and an enormous drive, someone who combines hustle, strategic creativity, and genuine curiosity about what makes businesses tick.

You might come from a classic sales background, or you might have built your commercial instincts in a completely different arena. What matters far more than your CV is your drive, your entrepreneurial instinct, and the kind of work ethic that makes people wonder how you get so much done.

In a single day you might: map a new industry vertical for outreach opportunities, run a consultative discovery call with a Head of Operations at a manufacturing company, develop a proposal for a new channel, follow up on an active deal in scoping, and draft a business case for entering a completely new market.

You won't have a large team behind you. You will have full autonomy, meaningful equity, direct access to the founding team, and the freedom to experiment with what works.

Why Lleverage?

  • Change the world, literally: 2026 is the year AI works, and Lleverage.ai has the best AI platform (according to industry veterans)

  • Work, learn, have fun: You'll be part of a top-notch commercial team that operates at the highest level of performance

  • Build a unique network: Connect with decision-makers and operational leaders across traditional industries who are eager to implement AI solutions

  • Get autonomy & ownership: Design your own strategies and own your pipeline development

  • Compensation: We pay top of market cash and equity, with compensation tied to the pipeline value you create

Responsibilities

  • Own our top of funnel: which segments we go after, how we reach the COOs and CFOs of manufacturers and distributors, and how many qualified opportunities land in the pipeline every week. That's your number.

  • Sit in on live deals from day one: discovery calls, account plans, proposals and PoC scoping with our delivery team. Within 6 to 12 months you run your first deals yourself.

  • Bring what you see in the market to the founding team and product: which use cases, sectors, competitors and prices we should bet on next.


Job specific requirements

  • 1 to 3 years in consulting, investment banking, PE or a fast-growing B2B startup, or you built something yourself.

Nice to haves

Our Tech Stack

You'll be working with best-in-class tools:

  • CRM: HubSpot for pipeline management

  • Communication: Multi-channel outreach across email, LinkedIn, and phone

  • And always exploring what's next

We offer

You are ready for the ride of a lifetime with experienced entrepreneurs and innovators who aim for hyper growth on a global scale. We look for an enormous drive and hands-on mentality. Somebody who can work with us in creating the best AI platform out there!

We offer a good salary, a highly experienced (and very entertaining...) team and considerable share and bonus packages. And last but not least, this is the start of your career to grow to into a commercial lead and to lay the foundation for years to come.

title: Graduate Silicon Architect 2027
descriptionHtml:
Location: Bristol, UK
Salary: £45,000 per annum 
Start date: September 2027
Application deadline: Midnight, 29th November 2026 
We encourage you to apply early, as we may close applications before the advertised deadline.

The Graduate Programme at Graphcore

Join Graphcore in a permanent role and start your career with two years of hands-on learning. From day one, you’ll be trusted to take ownership, share your ideas and help shape what we’re creating. You’ll tackle challenging problems alongside a team who support your development and are as excited about your success as you are.

What you’ll work on 

Put your understanding of computer architecture to work on the choices that shape Graphcore’s next generation of AI hardware. 

As a Graduate Silicon Architect, you’ll help specify, model and evaluate complex system-on-chip (SoC) subsystems, with guidance from experienced architects. You’ll explore how product requirements translate into technical options, design trade-offs and validation plans. 

Your work will likely include some of: taking responsibility for the architecture of a chip subsystem or function, modelling architectural features, assessing third-party intellectual property (IP) and supporting silicon bring-up. Working across design, verification, hardware and software teams, you’ll help gather the performance evidence that supports architecture decisions. 

Your team and support 

The Silicon Architecture team sits within the Silicon group. We stand for practical ambition: clear thinking, careful engineering and curiosity that improves real systems. 

You’ll work with mentors and experienced architects through design reviews, modelling, simulation, documentation and discussions with neighbouring teams. You’ll take ownership of defined tasks that grow in scope as you develop your skills. 

Simulations, performance data and design constraints help guide our decisions. You’ll be encouraged to ask questions, challenge existing approaches and share ideas for making things better. Take responsibility for your work and speak up when something needs testing, explaining or support. 

How you’ll learn and grow 

During the two-year programme, you’ll develop your architecture skills through hands-on architectural design + integration, modelling and evaluation of AI acceleration hardware, supported by mentors. 

Exploring technical options and running simulations will help you understand how architecture choices affect system behaviour. You’ll learn how to compare trade-offs, document findings and use performance evidence to support a decision. 

Design reviews and work across engineering teams will help you connect specifications to implementation and validation. Supporting silicon bring-up will give you experience of how architectural ideas are checked on real hardware, while tasks that grow in scope will build your technical judgement and confidence. 

What we’re looking for 

  • A degree, or expected degree, in Electronic Engineering, Computer Science or a related field 
  • An understanding of computer architecture or digital systems, with an interest in SoC design, AI hardware or high-performance computing 
  • Programming experience in Python, Rust, C++ or a similar language 
  • Analytical problem-solving skills and clear written and verbal communication, including documenting findings and explaining technical ideas 

You can demonstrate these skills through coursework, a dissertation, personal or team projects, research, or other relevant experience. Tell us what you built or investigated, how you approached it and what you learned. 

Exposure to register-transfer level (RTL) design, modelling, simulation, PCIe, Ethernet or DDR would be useful. These are additional strengths, rather than essential requirements. 

Benefits

  • Flexible working: Balance your work and personal life with greater flexibility
  • Retirement planning support: Up to 5% matched pension
  • Phantom equity: Share in Graphcore’s success
  • Workplace experience: Enjoy thoughtfully designed office spaces for collaboration, with free food and an on-site barista to support your day
  • Peace of mind protection: Income protection and life assurance to provide financial security for you and your loved ones
  • Electric Vehicle Scheme: Choose an electric vehicle and lease it through salary sacrifice
  • Flexible benefits: Tailor your benefits package with a choice of additional options, including private medical insurance and dental cover
  • Optional benefits: Dental cover, health cash plan, private medical insurance, cycle to work scheme, give as you earn

We welcome people from all backgrounds and experiences and are committed to building an inclusive environment where everyone can do their best work.

We’re an equal opportunity employer and recognise that everyone brings different strengths and perspectives. If you need any adjustments during the interview process, just let us know - we’re happy to support you.

Sponsorship

Applicants must already have the right to work in the UK for the full duration of the programme, without requiring visa sponsorship. We are unable to sponsor work visas for our Early Careers opportunities.

Introduction to Graphcore

At Graphcore, we’re building next generation AI compute: from semiconductors and software to systems at datacenter scale. We are proud to be owned by SoftBank Group and work with other companies in the SoftBank family to deliver AI compute to customers working at the AI frontier. Starting your career here means working alongside people with different backgrounds and expertise, from AI researchers to chip designers and software engineers. You’ll learn from each other, bring fresh ideas and help solve challenging problems together.

How to apply and what to expect 

To apply, answer the application questions below and upload your CV and cover letter. We’ll let you know the outcome of your application by early December at the latest. If successful, you’ll be invited to complete a technical assessment. Candidates who reach the final stage will then be invited to attend in-person assessments in early spring.

Ready to put your learning into practice? Start your career in a permanent SoC Architecture Engineer role, with two years of hands-on learning through the Graphcore Graduate Programme. Apply now and help shape what comes next.

title: GRC Engineer
descriptionHtml:
A little about us

incident.io is the AI software reliability platform trusted by engineering teams at Notion, Linear, Ramp and 2,000+ companies who can't afford downtime.

The stakes are real, the talent is insane, and somehow it's a genuinely lovely place to work. We all pull our weight, go the extra mile, and put in the bit of magic most companies don't have time for, all while having fun and never taking ourselves too seriously.

We've raised $100+ million from Index Ventures, Insight Partners, and Point Nine, and we're growing fast. There's never been a better time to join.

The role in one line

Being a GRC Engineer at incident.io means turning compliance from spreadsheets and screenshots into something that just runs, so “can you prove it?” gets answered before anyone asks.

What that looks like day to day

As a GRC Engineer at incident.io, you own how we prove we’re doing the right thing: our compliance programme, our customer security questionnaires, and the evidence behind both. One day you’re building an AI workflow that drafts questionnaire answers, the next you’re pushing our ISO 27001 work forward, the next you’re telling the product team what makes GRC painful.

Our GRC programme is young, and Slack is our system of record. You’ll make it scale, using AI-powered tooling and workflows to take the toil out of audits, evidence collection and customer questions.

Right now, that means:

  • ISO 27001. It’s in progress, and you’ll help raise the bar and get us over the line.

  • ISO 42001. We build AI products, so we want to manage AI responsibly. In your first two quarters or so, you’ll run a gap assessment against the standard.

  • Dogfooding. We use incident.io for our own security work, and you’ll drive product improvements that make GRC less painful for our customers too.

You’ll work closely with the wider security team, engineering, legal and product.

Who you are

  • You’ve run or contributed to a real compliance programme, ideally ISO 27001, and you know what it takes to get through an audit.

  • You’d rather automate evidence collection than chase people for screenshots.

  • You write code (Python, Go or similar) or build workflows, and you’re excited about using AI and agents to remove toil.

  • You can answer customer security questionnaires quickly, accurately and in plain English.

  • You can explain a control to an engineer and a risk to an executive, and both come away knowing what to do next.

  • You care about the product, and you’ll tell us what’s missing from our own GRC tooling.

  • You’re comfortable with high autonomy. Nobody’s going to hand you a detailed spec, you’re trusted to figure out what needs doing and just do it.

  • Bonus points for ISO 42001 or AI governance experience, SOC 2, GDPR, or time in a fast-growing SaaS company.

Supporting you

We work hard and we think life outside work matters just as much. Our benefits pack is built to support both.

  • Private medical insurance. Seriously good cover - we want you and the people you love to be looked after.

  • Competitive annual leave. Showing up at your best requires switching off, and we make sure you have time to do that.

  • First Friday of every month off. Yes, seriously.

  • Enhanced pension. We put real money in, because future-you deserves better than an afterthought.

  • Meaningful equity. We’re rapidly scaling, and everyone who helps shape the outcome should share in it.

  • Unlimited AI spend. For everyone, not just engineers. We’re all-in on AI across the company, and we expect you to be too.

  • Generous parental leave. The early days with a new baby matter more than anything we’re doing here, and we want you to be present for them.

  • Two budgets that have your back. £1000 to invest in your setup, £500 a year to invest in yourself.

title: Group Director of Supply Chain
descriptionHtml:

Our goal is clear: to protect and improve the environment by effectively managing refrigerants throughout their entire lifecycle.

The Group Director, Supply Chain is accountable for designing and leading A-Gas's global supply chain, strategic sourcing and Sales, Inventory and Operations Planning (SIOP) capability. The role will create an integrated view of demand, supply, inventory and third-party spend to secure critical supply, improve service, optimise inventory and working capital, reduce total cost and enable better commercial and operational decisions. Desirable

Because your work contributes to something bigger:

descriptionHtml:

- Own the global capacity model for Tier 1, Tier 2, showroom and Customer Service fallback coverage, run the monthly refresh and seasonal peak plan, and flag hiring, reallocation or BPO volume changes early while tracking planned versus actual coverage with Sales Leads and Finance.

title: Head of AI Factory Commissioning
descriptionHtml:
Firmus Technologies

Firmus Technologies is a global leader pioneering the development and operation of efficient AI infrastructure across Asia Pacific.  

Founded in Australia in 2019, our mission is to create the most efficient AI infrastructure by combining cutting-edge technology with a steadfast commitment to sustainability. 

At Firmus, we are unique in our approach. We design, build, and operate a new class of digital infrastructure – the AI Factory. Through our model-to-grid technology approach, we have pushed the boundaries of multi-generational liquid cooling systems, energy management, AI software orchestration, and construction. For our customers, this approach allows us to make every watt count and deliver low-cost AI tokens globally. 

Firmus AI Cloud

Our large-scale GPU cloud platform, Firmus AI Cloud, is purpose-built to deliver energy-efficient AI compute at scale to customers. 

It empowers developers, enterprises, educational institutions, and government users to train and deploy AI models with unmatched efficiency and cost savings. With an ever-growing suite of services and applications, we are committed to delivering a cloud experience that is market-leading, proprietary, and built to scale. 

Role Summary

Firmus Technologies is seeking a Head of AI Factory Commissioning to build and lead the function responsible for commissioning the physical infrastructure of our AI Factories across the Asia Pacific region. You will set the strategy, standards and governance that ensure every AI Factory is proven safe, resilient and performing to design before any compute is deployed.

An AI Factory is a building scale computer that places unprecedented demands on power density, liquid cooling, controls integration, operational resilience, and commissioning rigor. This role is responsible for ensuring these next-generation facilities are proven ready to support large-scale GPU deployments before handover to AI Cluster Commissioning. Firmus has AI factories under development ranging in size from tens of MW to GW scale.

This is a function lead role, at the same level as the Head of AI Cluster Commissioning. You will lead a team of Commissioning Managers who run the day-to-day commissioning. Your focus will be building the function, setting direction, managing risk across the portfolio, and owning the “ready for IT” gate: no data hall is handed over for cluster bring-up until its infrastructure has passed the appropriate level of commissioning acceptance.

Key Responsibilities

Leadership & Function Build

  • Build, lead and develop a high-performing team of Commissioning Managers and commissioning professionals.
  • Define the structure, capability and resourcing model for the function so it can scale with Firmus’ national and APAC project pipeline.
  • Allocate leadership and resources across the portfolio of AI Factory projects, balancing priorities and managing delivery risk.
  • Build a culture of safety, ownership, technical rigour and continuous improvement.

Commissioning Strategy & Governance

  • Set the strategic direction for AI Factory commissioning, including the methodology, commissioning levels (L1–L5), Integrated Systems Testing (IST) approach and acceptance criteria.
  • Direct the development of commissioning standards, frameworks and templates, delivered through the Commissioning Manager.
  • Set up governance, assurance and reporting that give leadership clear visibility of commissioning progress, readiness and quality across all projects.
  • Make sure commissioning strategies cover all critical infrastructure, including:
    • HV/MV/LV power distribution, UPS, generators and battery energy storage
    • Liquid cooling (CDUs, secondary fluid networks, chillers and heat rejection)
    • Air-side cooling (CRAH/CRAC units, fan walls, air handling and containment)
    • Controls and monitoring: BMS, EPMS and the CubeSense SCADA platform
    • Fire detection and suppression, security and other life-safety systems
  • Act as the final escalation point for complex technical issues, commissioning failures and acceptance decisions.

Handover & Stakeholder Interfaces

  • Own the facility “ready for IT” gate, jointly with the Head of AI Cluster Commissioning, so commissioned data halls hand over cleanly to cluster bring-up.
  • Set the standard for handover to operations, including as-built documentation, training, known issues and operational readiness.
  • Work with Engineering & Technology, Construction/Delivery, Operations and the AI Infrastructure Platform (AIIP) teams to embed commissionability from concept design onwards.
  • Represent commissioning with executive leadership, customers, partners and key suppliers.

Commercial, Performance & Continuous Improvement

  • Set the strategy for engaging third-party commissioning agents and oversee their commercial and delivery performance.
  • Own the commissioning budget and oversee schedule, cost and risk across the portfolio.
  • Drive the use of digital commissioning platforms, automation and data-driven validation, so each AI Factory is commissioned faster and more repeatably than the last.
  • Make sure design performance (PUE, thermal and resilience) is validated, and feed lessons learned back into Firmus’ AI Factory designs and standards.

Skills & Experience

Häufige Fragen zum Loom-Video im Bewerbungsprozess

Wenn du dich bei uns bewirbst möchten wir ein Loom Video von dir erhalten. 🙏🏻

Warum wollt ihr ein Video statt eines Anschreibens? Weil wir in der Content-Branche arbeiten und uns ein kurzes Video in zwei Minuten mehr über dich sagt als jedes Anschreiben.

Was ist Loom und brauche ich einen Account? Loom ist ein kostenloses Tool, mit dem du dich selbst und/oder deinen Bildschirm aufnimmst und per Link teilst. Die kostenlose Version reicht völlig. Du kannst auch jedes andere Tool nutzen (z. B. Handyvideo über Google Drive) Hauptsache, wir können den Link öffnen.

Wie lang sollte das Video sein? 2–4 Minuten. Kürzer ist besser als länger – wenn du es knapp auf den Punkt bringst, ist das schon ein Pluspunkt.

Was soll ich im Video sagen? Stell dich kurz vor, erzähl, warum du zu RealStudio willst, und zeig uns ein Projekt, einen Kunden oder ein Ergebnis, auf das du stolz bist. Gerne mit geteiltem Bildschirm, z. B. Kampagnen, Reportings oder Content, an dem du beteiligt warst.

Muss das Video professionell aussehen? Nein. Kein Schnitt, keine Musik, kein Skript nötig. Wir bewerten nicht die Videoqualität, sondern dich. Ein ruhiger Ort und guter Ton reichen.

Auf Deutsch oder Englisch? Bitte auf Deutsch, da unsere Kunden überwiegend aus dem DACH-Raum kommen.

Wer sieht mein Video? Nur die Personen, die bei uns am Bewerbungsprozess beteiligt sind. Wir teilen es nicht weiter und löschen es nach Abschluss des Verfahrens.

Wie geht es nach dem Video weiter? Wir melden uns innerhalb von max 2 Werktagen bei dir. Wenn es passt, folgt ein Kennenlern-Call und danach ein Probetag, an dem du an einer realistischen Aufgabe mit uns arbeitest.

title: Head of Capital
descriptionHtml:
Relay is fundamentally reshaping how goods move in an online era. Backed by Europe’s largest-ever logistics Series A ($35M) led by deep-tech investors Plural, and a recently closed Series B ($95M), Relay is scaling faster than 99% of venture-backed startups. We're assembling the most talent-dense team the logistics industry has ever seen

Relay’s Mission is to free commerce from friction. Today, high delivery costs act as a hidden tax on e-commerce, quietly shaping what can be sold online and limiting who can participate. We envision a world where more goods move more freely between more people, making the online shopping experience seamless and accessible to everyone.

THE TEAM
• ~160 people, around half in engineering, product and data
• 45+ advanced degrees across computer science, mathematics and operations research
• Thousands of data points captured, calculated, analysed and predicted for every single parcel we handle
• An intellectually vibrant culture of first‑principles thinking, tight feedback loops and relentless experimentation

The opportunity

We are looking for a Head of Capital to run how Relay raises equity and works with its investors: the next round and the ones after it, from the investor map to the close, next to the CEO.

Relay is a technology enabled parcel carrier - we deliver parcels from retailers to end customers but do it much more efficiently than incumbents. This efficiency has propelled us into one of the fastest growing companies in Europe - we have grown over 40x in the last 18 months. The capital Relay raises decides how fast the network grows and what it can promise retailers. Raising it well, from the right investors, on terms we understand, is a job in its own right.

About the role

The capital we raise next decides how fast the network grows and what it can promise retailers. Our next round is planned for Q2/Q3 2027. It is for growth, from growth-stage investors, and it will be won on evidence. Today a raise runs through the CEO and the CFO alongside their day jobs. It works. It is however, not a system.

You will be the person who makes it one. You will not just be the person who holds and runs the Series C transaction, but also be the Head of the Office that will build the systems to raise multiple rounds of capital in the future. Between rounds you keep the map, the materials and the investors warm, so each raise starts from a record, not a blank page. Few roles let you own how a growing company raises the capital it runs on, from the inside, round after round.

Who you work with

  • CEO: you report here. The CEO pitches and takes the decisions on a round.

  • CFO: you work together daily. The CFO owns the budget, the forecast, internal finance and any debt. You own equity, the investors behind it, and the investor-facing model built from the CFO's numbers — never a second set.

  • Co-founder and the Extended Leadership Team: the proof a round needs.

  • External & Internal Counsel: terms and the close.

  • Board: updates between rounds and approval on the round.

What you'll do

Running the transaction with the CEO & CFO

  1. Build the investor map: which funds, which partner at each, why each fits us, in what order we go, and the warm path to each.

  2. The process start to close: the timeline, outreach, a brief before every meeting and notes after, investor questions answered within a day, and diligence.

  3. Put term sheets side by side and show what each costs in the round after. Draw up illustrative analysis and counsel the CEO on the right strategy.

  4. Hold the story in one version, drafted with the CEO. The same claims and numbers across the deck, the model and the data room.

  5. Own the investor-facing model: scenarios, unit economics and use of funds. Every number ties to one the CFO has signed.

Between rounds

  1. Refresh the deck, the KPI pack and the data room every quarter.

  2. Write investor and board updates. Answer existing investors' questions. Track what we promised them.

  3. Build relationships with investors so you can source your own relationships for future rounds

  4. Read the market: who invests at our stage, on what terms, and what comparable companies showed when they raised. Put what Relay must show, and by when, to the leadership team in writing.

Across both

  1. Agree in writing with each function what it produces for a raise and by when. Flag the proof the story needs a quarter early, not the week before.

  2. Keep the record: what each investor asked, what we answered, what we promised and what we learned.

By the end of your first six months

  • An investor map with a reason beside every name.

  • One version of the story across the deck, the model and the data room.

  • A data room refreshed every quarter, never rebuilt.

  • A written agreement with each function on what it produces for a raise.

  • A clear line of sight to a closed round from a ranked list of investors.

What we're looking for

You have run a growth-stage equity round from inside a company, or worked on several from the investing side. You want to own the process, with a view to owning the pitch and fundraising function in the future as the company scales.

We don't ask for a set number of years or a particular firm on your CV. We ask for evidence. Be ready to walk us through specific rounds and your part in them.

Required

  • Round experience: you ran an equity round from inside a company, or worked on several as an investor. You can show the map you built, the order you ran it in and what you would change.

  • Investor writing: you turn the story a founder tells in a room into a page an investor reads alone. Short, plain, in a founder's voice, with numbers that held under diligence.

  • Modelling: you built an investor model from a company's internal forecast and defended it in diligence.

  • Terms: you can put two term sheets side by side and say what each costs in the round after.

  • Data rooms: you built one that answered questions before they were asked. You can name the question you missed.

  • Getting work from other teams: you got inputs from teams that did not report to you, on dates agreed in writing. You can say what arrived late and what you did about it.

  • Market knowledge: you know which funds invest at our stage and which partner leads, or can build that picture in weeks and show your working.

  • Handling no: investors have told you no. You kept the record of why and used it the next time.

Nice to have

  • Experience in logistics, delivery, marketplaces or another operations-heavy business.

  • Time at a growth-stage fund, a tech-focused bank or a private-capital adviser before going in-house.

  • Investor relations between rounds at a private company.

The hard parts

  • The CEO pitches. You are the investors' contact for everything around the room. You are judged on how the round runs, not on the pitch.

  • The numbers come from the CFO. The proof comes from teams that do not report to you.

  • The market sets the timing, not us.

  • Investors will say no, often. The record has to stay straight.

  • The job keeps going after the close: the map, the materials in quiet quarters and the relationships between rounds. We will agree with you what support you need to do that well.

How we hire

  1. Talent Acquisition, 45 minutes: the job as it is, a round you ran or worked on, and how you work.

  2. An interview with our VP International: 45 minutes: how you work, the evidence and across your whole career

  3. The case, about a day on your own time

  4. Case review, 75 minutes, with the CEO and CFO: you walk us through it, re-plan live when we change a condition, and take two questions the case cannot reach .

  5. References and a decision within a week. An offer comes in a conversation.

Tell us at any stage if you need adjustments.

Who Thrives at Relay?

  • Aim with Precision: You define problems clearly and measure your impact meticulously.

  • Play to Win: You chase bold bets, tackle the hard stuff, and view constraints as fuel, not friction.

  • 1% Better Every Day: You believe that small, consistent improvements lead to exponential growth. You move quickly, deliver results, and learn from every experience.

  • All In, All the Time: You show up and step up. You take ownership from start to finish and do what it takes to deliver when it counts.

  • People-Powered Greatness: You invest in your teammates. You give and receive feedback with care and candour. You build trust through high standards and shared success.

  • Grow the Whole Pie: You seek out win-win solutions for merchants, couriers, and our customers, because when they thrive, so do we.

    If these resonate, and you combine strong technical fundamentals with entrepreneurial drive, let’s connect.

Relay is an equal-opportunity employer committed to diversity, inclusion, and fostering a workplace where everyone thrives.

title: Head of Compliance – SMF16
descriptionHtml:
About BJAK

BJAK is Southeast Asia’s largest digital insurance platform, expanding financial access through automation, data, and digital scale. As we grow across markets, we are committed to building a platform that is safe, compliant, and trusted.

We are hiring a Head of Compliance – SMF16 to lead regulatory strategy, risk governance, and compliance operations for our UK market entry and expansion alongside the CEO. This role is expected to hold the SMF16 (Compliance Oversight) Senior Management Function once approved, and will act as our primary point of contact with the FCA.

This is a build role: you'll be creating frameworks, policies, and controls from scratch rather than inheriting an existing function.

 

Why This Role Matters

The Head of Compliance – SMF16 will:

  • Design and enforce compliance frameworks that enable safe scaling of digital financial services.

  • Ensure BJAK operates in accordance with UK regulatory standards, especially FCA requirements.

  • Protect consumers through transparent, fair, and ethical practices.

  • Establish BJAK as a trusted partner with regulators, partners, and industry stakeholders.

  • Build compliance capability and culture across the company.

 

What You Will Do

Regulatory Leadership & Strategy

  • Develop and maintain compliance frameworks aligned with UK regulatory requirements.

  • Lead regulatory readiness for market entry, licensing, and ongoing supervision.

  • Serve as the primary contact with the FCA and relevant UK bodies.

  • Interpret regulatory changes and guide business strategy accordingly.

 

Risk Governance & Compliance Operations

  • Build policies and controls covering AML, KYC, data privacy, consumer duty, distribution, and claims-related compliance.

  • Conduct risk assessments and implement remediation plans for identified gaps.

  • Establish monitoring, testing, and reporting processes for ongoing compliance.

  • Ensure internal audits, compliance reviews, and control testing are operationalised.

 

Consumer Protection & Business Integrity

  • Embed fairness, transparency, and responsible selling throughout the organisation.

  • Oversee product compliance, marketing reviews, pricing governance, and distribution oversight.

  • Implement complaint handling frameworks aligned with regulatory standards.

 

Cross-Functional Support & Training

  • Partner with product, operations, legal, marketing, and commercial teams to ensure compliant execution.

  • Provide guidance on regulatory implications of new products, partnerships, or distribution models.

  • Deliver training to ensure teams understand and execute compliance responsibilities.

 

You Will Thrive in This Role If You

  • See compliance as a strategic enabler, not a blocker.

  • Operate with high integrity, sound judgment, and strong attention to detail.

  • Communicate clearly and influence leaders using data and logic.

  • Enjoy building frameworks and scaling systems from early-stage to mature environments.

  • Thrive in fast-paced, evolving settings where regulation meets innovation.

 

What You Bring

  • 8+ years of compliance, risk, or regulatory experience within financial services, insurance, insurtech, or fintech.

  • Deep understanding of UK regulatory frameworks, including FCA rules and consumer duty requirements.

  • Experience in compliance for digital platforms, distribution, or insurance products (preferred).

  • Proven ability to design policies, conduct risk assessments, and manage complex compliance programs.

  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, including dealing with regulators.

 

Bonus (Nice to Have)

  • Experience in start-up or high-growth environments.

  • Previous SMF experience.

  • Background in insurtech, digital distribution, or online marketplaces.

  • Knowledge of GDPR, AML, sanctions, or cross-border compliance.

 

Location Requirement

  • This role is based in the UK. This is a hybrid role. You are expected to work from our London office at least 3 days per week.

 

Why Join Us

  • Shape compliance for a fast-growing international fintech-insurtech platform.

  • Build frameworks that enable safe, inclusive financial access at scale.

  • Work closely with leadership and regulators to drive responsible innovation.

  • Competitive compensation with long-term growth and international career opportunities.


Compensations Range

  • We offer a highly competitive package, ranging from £100,000 to £150,000, reflecting both experience and suitability for this pivotal role.
